title: Studio English Foundations I: Garments, Tools, and Classroom Language
description: A first-semester ESP module that introduces fashion-study identity language, studio routines, garment vocabulary, visual description, and short portfolio-ready writing.

module_manifest.title: Studio English Foundations I: Garments, Tools, and Classroom Language
module_manifest.description: A first-semester ESP module that introduces fashion-study identity language, studio routines, garment vocabulary, visual description, and short portfolio-ready writing.
learning_goals: Build beginner-accessible English routines connected to Fashion Design coursework.
Develop confidence with core studio vocabulary, simple descriptions, and guided self-introductions.
Prepare learners to produce short written and spoken design-related outputs.
professional_outcomes: Students can explain who they are as Fashion Design students in simple English.
Students can understand and use recurring studio and coursework vocabulary.
Students can begin building short portfolio-friendly written artifacts.
language_outcomes: Use sentence frames for self-introduction, preference, and learning goals.
Recognize high-frequency course, studio, and design vocabulary.
Write short guided responses with clear meaning and basic accuracy.

weeks.title: Welcome to Fashion Design English
weeks.summary: Students learn the Week 1 course rhythm, complete a light diagnostic, build starter vocabulary for Fashion Design study, and produce a short bilingual-supported English profile they can reuse in later speaking and portfolio work.
weeks.essential_question: How can English help me introduce myself and participate in Fashion Design study from the first week?

week_manifest.title: Welcome to Fashion Design English
week_manifest.summary: Students learn the Week 1 course rhythm, complete a light diagnostic, build starter vocabulary for Fashion Design study, and produce a short bilingual-supported English profile they can reuse in later speaking and portfolio work.
week_manifest.essential_question: How can English help me introduce myself and participate in Fashion Design study from the first week?
week_manifest.professional_context: Week 1 connects English directly to first-semester Fashion Design routines, including drawing, sewing, patternmaking, creativity, text production, and the habit of explaining personal interests and study goals in a studio context.
grammar_focus: I am a fashion design student
teacher_preparation: Review the Week 1 manual sequence and keep the tone welcoming, visual, and low-pressure.
Preview the reading text, listening script, and vocabulary image set before class.
Prepare a pronunciation list for fashion design, sketch, fabric, garment, sewing, patternmaking, studio, and portfolio.
Decide whether students will draft the profile on paper, in a shared document, or in a future app text-response field.
Plan how to monitor the teacher-led speaking session and note which students need extra support with sentence frames.
student_deliverables: Completion of the orientation and diagnostic task.
Reading-comprehension responses about a model Fashion Design student.
Listening-comprehension responses about a first-semester Fashion Design student.
Completion of the starter vocabulary practice set.
A 50-80 word Fashion Design student profile in English.
One corrected sentence saved after feedback review.
A short oral self-introduction during the teacher-led session.

activities.title: Start Here: Your Fashion English Course
activities.summary: Students meet the weekly rhythm of the course, complete a light self-assessment, and connect English to real Fashion Design study goals.

en.title: Start Here: Your Fashion English Course

en.instructions: Read the welcome screen, look at the weekly routine, and answer the short diagnostic questions about your interests and goals.

activities.title: Build Your Fashion Student Profile
activities.summary: Students produce the first reusable written artifact of the course: a short profile about who they are, what they study, and why they want English for Fashion Design.

en.title: Build Your Fashion Student Profile

en.instructions: Use the sentence frames and Week 1 vocabulary to build a short profile with four core sentences about who you are, what you like, and why you want English.

sentence_frames: I am a Fashion Design student.

rubric.needs_work_pt: O perfil precisa de vocabulário de Design de Moda mais preciso ou mais específico.

assessment.model_response_en: My name is Mariana. I am a Fashion Design student. I like sketching garments. I want English for fashion vocabulary and portfolio texts.
assessment.model_response_pt: Meu nome é Mariana. Eu sou estudante de Design de Moda. Eu gosto de fazer croquis de roupas. Eu quero inglês para vocabulário de moda e textos de portfólio.
common_errors: Missing the verb in I am.
Using Portuguese word order in English sentences.
Writing a very general goal with no Fashion Design context.
feedback_prompts_en: Can you add one clearer Fashion Design detail?
Can you improve one sentence with I am, I study, or I want to?
Please revise one sentence and resubmit after teacher feedback.
feedback_prompts_pt: Você pode acrescentar um detalhe mais claro de Design de Moda?
Você pode melhorar uma frase usando I am, I like ou I want English for?
Revise uma frase e envie novamente depois do feedback do professor.

support: Allow students to build the profile from a sentence bank before writing independently.
challenge: Invite students to add one sentence about a future design area such as accessories, styling, or sustainability.

extension_options: Turn the written profile into a 20 to 30 second spoken introduction for the live session.
activities.notes_for_app_design: Render this as a teacher-reviewed structured writing submission with saved sentence-frame fields for the four core profile lines. Show the teacher the completed profile, required-elements checklist, Week 1 rubric, common-error prompts, teacher feedback tools, and a return-for-revision action. Save the first submission and any revised resubmission.

activities.title: Review and Improve One Sentence
activities.summary: Students begin the course correction habit by reviewing a common Week 1 sentence problem and saving one improved version.

en.title: Review and Improve One Sentence
en.summary: Look at a corrected sentence and write the improved version clearly.
en.instructions: Choose one correction card, study the model, and rewrite the improved sentence in English.
success_criteria: I can identify one problem in a sentence.
I can rewrite one sentence more clearly.
I can use the correction to improve my own writing.
sentence_frames: I am a Fashion Design student.

pt.title: Revise e melhore uma frase
pt.summary: Observe uma frase corrigida e escreva a versão melhorada com clareza.
pt.instructions: Escolha um cartão de correção, observe o modelo e reescreva a frase melhorada em inglês.
success_criteria: Eu consigo identificar um problema em uma frase.
Eu consigo reescrever uma frase com mais clareza.
Eu consigo usar a correção para melhorar minha própria escrita.
sentence_frames: I am a Fashion Design student.

activities.teacher_instructions: Use common Week 1 errors that students are likely to produce. Keep the focus narrow: one corrected sentence and one clear reason for the change.

input.prompt_en: Rewrite one corrected Week 1 sentence clearly and accurately.
input.prompt_pt: Reescreva com clareza e precisão uma frase corrigida da Semana 1.

items.label_en: Correct the sentence about student identity.
items.label_pt: Corrija a frase sobre identidade de estudante.
items.correct_sentence: I am a Fashion Design student.
accepted_answers: I am a Fashion Design student.

items.label_en: Correct the sentence about learning goals.
items.label_pt: Corrija a frase sobre objetivos de aprendizagem.
Corrija a frase sobre interesses.

steps.title: Choose a correction card
steps.student_action_en: Read the original sentence and the corrected model.
steps.student_action_pt: Leia a frase original e o modelo corrigido.
steps.teacher_action: Explain the error focus briefly: missing article, missing verb, or infinitive after want.

steps.title: Rewrite the sentence
steps.student_action_en: Write the improved version of the sentence clearly in English.
steps.student_action_pt: Escreva a versão melhorada da frase com clareza em inglês.
steps.teacher_action: Ask students to notice how the correction can help their own profile writing.

steps.title: Connect the correction to your work
steps.student_action_en: Check whether your own profile needs the same correction.
steps.student_action_pt: Confira se o seu próprio perfil precisa da mesma correção.
steps.teacher_action: Prompt students to edit one sentence in their profile if needed.

expected_output.description_en: One corrected and rewritten Week 1 sentence.
expected_output.description_pt: Uma frase da Semana 1 corrigida e reescrita.

completion_criteria_en: The student chooses one correction card.
The student rewrites the sentence accurately.
The student checks whether the same issue appears in their own writing.
completion_criteria_pt: O aluno escolhe um cartão de correção.
O aluno reescreve a frase corretamente.
O aluno verifica se o mesmo problema aparece na própria escrita.
checklist_en: I studied one corrected model.
I rewrote one sentence.
I checked my own profile for the same problem.
checklist_pt: Eu observei um modelo corrigido.
Eu reescrevi uma frase.
Eu verifiquei meu próprio perfil para o mesmo problema.
assessment.model_response_en: I am a Fashion Design student.
assessment.model_response_pt: I am a Fashion Design student.
common_errors: Copying the original incorrect sentence again.
Improving the sentence but keeping one target error.
feedback_prompts_en: Can you use the same correction in your own profile?
feedback_prompts_pt: Você pode usar a mesma correção no seu próprio perfil?

support: Limit the choice to two correction cards instead of three.
challenge: Ask students to explain the correction rule in simple language.

extension_options: Revise one additional sentence from your profile using the same grammar pattern.
activities.notes_for_app_design: Render this as a correction-card activity with one card shown at a time. The student opens one incorrect sentence, types or selects the corrected version, and gets an app check against accepted answers. Save one corrected sentence as the submitted mini-revision artifact and link it back to the Week 1 profile task for transfer.

activities.title: Teacher Session: Introductions and Course Routine
activities.summary: Students bring the week together in a teacher-led session focused on course rhythm, pronunciation, oral self-introduction, and one simple feedback move.

en.title: Teacher Session: Introductions and Course Routine
en.summary: Practice pronunciation, introduce yourself, and use your Week 1 profile in a live session.
en.instructions: Bring your profile, practice the key words, and give a short spoken introduction using the Week 1 sentence frames.
success_criteria: I can say a short introduction with support.
I can pronounce some key Fashion Design words clearly.
I can listen to one classmate and respond with a simple positive comment or question.
sentence_frames: I am a Fashion Design student.
I want to learn English for ___.

pt.title: Sessão com o professor: apresentações e rotina do curso
pt.summary: Pratique pronúncia, apresente-se e use o seu perfil da Semana 1 em uma sessão ao vivo.
pt.instructions: Leve o seu perfil, pratique as palavras principais e faça uma apresentação oral curta usando as frases-modelo da Semana 1.
success_criteria: Eu consigo fazer uma apresentação curta com apoio.
Eu consigo pronunciar algumas palavras importantes de Moda com clareza.
Eu consigo ouvir um colega e responder com um comentário positivo curto ou uma pergunta.
sentence_frames: I am a Fashion Design student.
I want to learn English for ___.

activities.teacher_instructions: Use the live session to reinforce confidence, pronunciation, and course navigation. Students may read from their profile first, then try a more natural version. Include one very light feedback phrase so critique language begins gently without turning Week 1 into a full critique lesson.

input.prompt_en: Use your Week 1 profile to introduce yourself in the teacher session.
input.prompt_pt: Use o seu perfil da Semana 1 para se apresentar na sessão com o professor.

items.label_en: Say your name, your study area, one interest, and one English goal.
items.label_pt: Diga o seu nome, sua área de estudo, um interesse e um objetivo de inglês.

items.label_en: Respond to one classmate with a simple comment or question.
items.label_pt: Responda a um colega com um comentário simples ou uma pergunta.

steps.title: Review the course rhythm
steps.student_action_en: Listen to the teacher's explanation of how the weekly routine works and ask questions if needed.
steps.student_action_pt: Escute a explicação do professor sobre como a rotina semanal funciona e faça perguntas se necessário.
steps.teacher_action: Reinforce the weekly cycle and confirm that students know where to find tasks and feedback.

steps.title: Pronunciation clinic
steps.student_action_en: Repeat and practice key Week 1 words such as fashion design, sketch, fabric, garment, sewing, patternmaking, studio, and portfolio.
steps.student_action_pt: Repita e pratique palavras importantes da Semana 1 como fashion design, sketch, fabric, garment, sewing, patternmaking, studio e portfólio.
steps.teacher_action: Model the words slowly, then in natural connected speech.

steps.title: Guided introductions
steps.student_action_en: Use your profile to introduce yourself in 3 to 5 sentences.
steps.student_action_pt: Use o seu perfil para se apresentar em 3 a 5 frases.
steps.teacher_action: Allow students to read first if needed, then invite more natural delivery on a second try.

steps.title: Mini response and wrap-up
steps.student_action_en: Listen to one classmate and respond with a short positive comment or one simple question.
steps.student_action_pt: Escute um colega e responda com um comentário positivo curto ou uma pergunta simples.
steps.teacher_action: Keep the tone supportive and preview Week 2: The Fashion Studio.

expected_output.description_en: A short spoken introduction plus one simple response to a classmate.
expected_output.description_pt: Uma autoapresentação oral curta mais uma resposta simples a um colega.
expected_output.length_or_format: 20 to 40 seconds speaking plus one short response

completion_criteria_en: The student gives a short oral introduction using support.
The student's key Fashion Design words are understandable.
The student responds to one peer with a simple comment or question.
completion_criteria_pt: O aluno faz uma apresentação oral curta com apoio.
As palavras principais de Moda do aluno são compreensíveis.
O aluno responde a um colega com um comentário simples ou uma pergunta.
checklist_en: I brought my profile.
I practiced the key words.
I introduced myself.
I responded to one classmate.
checklist_pt: Eu levei o meu perfil.
Eu pratiquei as palavras principais.
Eu me apresentei.
Eu respondi a um colega.
assessment.model_response_en: My name is Julia. I am a Fashion Design student. I like sketching and fabric work. I am interested in accessories. I want to learn English for portfolio texts.
assessment.model_response_pt: Meu nome é Julia. Eu sou estudante de Design de Moda. Eu gosto de croquis e de trabalhar com tecido. Tenho interesse em acessórios. Quero aprender inglês para textos de portfólio.
common_errors: Dropping key verbs during speaking.
Speaking too quietly to be understood.
Giving a response with no clear Fashion Design detail.
feedback_prompts_en: Can you say that again with I am or I want to?
Can you add one more Fashion Design detail?
feedback_prompts_pt: Você pode dizer isso novamente usando I am ou I want to?
Você pode acrescentar mais um detalhe de Design de Moda?

support: Let students read directly from the written profile during the first round.
challenge: Ask stronger learners to answer one follow-up question and give one simple feedback phrase to a peer.

extension_options: Repeat your introduction with a partner and focus on one target pronunciation word after teacher feedback.
activities.notes_for_app_design: Keep this as a teacher-observed speaking activity with a completion checklist, sentence-frame prompt card, and teacher notes. Do not record or upload student audio. The app role is only to display the speaking prompt, track completion, and support teacher observation.

vocabulary_groups.title: Student identity and course routine
vocabulary_groups.description: Core words students need to explain who they are and how the weekly course works.

items.definition_en: A person who is studying in a school, course, or university.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A person who is learning in a class or course.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Uma pessoa que está aprendendo em uma aula, curso ou universidade.
items.example_sentence_en: I am a Fashion Design student.
items.example_sentence_pt: Eu sou estudante de Design de Moda.
items.professional_context_en: Students use this word to introduce themselves in class and in profile texts.
items.professional_context_pt: Os alunos usam essa palavra para se apresentar na aula e em textos de perfil.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução direta mais comum é 'estudante' ou 'aluno'.
items.pronunciation_notes: Say STU-dent with stress on the first syllable.

items.definition_en: A program of study with classes and tasks.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A set of classes that students follow to learn something.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um conjunto de aulas que os alunos fazem para aprender alguma coisa.
items.example_sentence_en: This course helps me learn English for Fashion Design.
items.example_sentence_pt: Este curso me ajuda a aprender inglês para Design de Moda.
items.professional_context_en: Week 1 uses this word to explain the ESP course routine and expectations.
items.professional_context_pt: A Semana 1 usa essa palavra para explicar a rotina e as expectativas do curso de ESP.
items.translation_notes_pt: Em contexto acadêmico, pode ser 'curso'.
items.pronunciation_notes: Say KORS as one syllable in most common models.

items.definition_en: To send work for review.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: To send your task or answer to the teacher or platform.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Enviar sua atividade ou resposta para o professor ou para a plataforma.
items.example_sentence_en: Submit your profile after you review one sentence.
items.example_sentence_pt: Envie o seu perfil depois de revisar uma frase.
items.professional_context_en: Students need this word for digital tasks, drafts, and weekly assignments.
items.professional_context_pt: Os alunos precisam dessa palavra para tarefas digitais, rascunhos e atividades semanais.
items.translation_notes_pt: Pode ser traduzido como 'enviar' ou 'submeter', dependendo do contexto.

items.definition_en: Comments that help improve work.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: Helpful comments about what is good and what can improve.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Comentários úteis sobre o que está bom e o que pode melhorar.
items.example_sentence_en: I read the feedback and improve one sentence.
items.example_sentence_pt: Eu leio o feedback e melhoro uma frase.
items.professional_context_en: Feedback is important in writing revision, critiques, and teacher review.
items.professional_context_pt: O feedback é importante na revisão de escrita, em críticas e na avaliação do professor.
items.translation_notes_pt: A forma 'feedback' é comum, mas 'devolutiva' também pode aparecer.
items.pronunciation_notes: Say FEED-back with stress on FEED.

items.definition_en: To look at work again carefully.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: To check your work again before or after feedback.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Verificar seu trabalho novamente antes ou depois do feedback.
items.example_sentence_en: Review your profile before you submit it.
items.example_sentence_pt: Revise o seu perfil antes de envia-lo.
items.professional_context_en: Review is part of revision habits in class and in portfolio preparation.
items.professional_context_pt: A revisão faz parte do hábito de melhorar textos na aula e na preparação de portfólio.
items.translation_notes_pt: Pode ser traduzido como 'revisar' ou 'analisar novamente'.

vocabulary_groups.title: Fashion-design identity
vocabulary_groups.description: Words students need to name their field and professional direction.

items.definition_en: The field of creating clothing, accessories, and fashion concepts.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: The subject students study when they learn to create fashion ideas and products.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: A área em que os alunos aprendem a criar ideias e produtos de moda.
items.example_sentence_en: I study Fashion Design at university.
items.example_sentence_pt: Eu estudo Design de Moda na universidade.
items.professional_context_en: Students use this phrase to explain their degree and professional area.
items.professional_context_pt: Os alunos usam essa expressão para explicar o curso e a área profissional.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais natural é 'Design de Moda'.
items.pronunciation_notes: Say FASH-un de-ZINE with clear stress on the second word.

items.definition_en: A person who creates fashion ideas, garments, or collections.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A person who plans and creates designs.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Uma pessoa que planeja e cria designs.
items.example_sentence_en: She wants to become a designer.
items.example_sentence_pt: Ela quer se tornar designer.
items.professional_context_en: The word helps students connect their studies to a future profession.
items.professional_context_pt: A palavra ajuda os alunos a relacionar os estudos a uma profissao futura.
items.translation_notes_pt: No uso cotidiano, 'designer' costuma ser mantido em inglês.
items.pronunciation_notes: Say de-ZY-ner with stress on ZY.

items.definition_en: A workspace for making, studying, or discussing design work.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A place where design students work, practice, and create.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um lugar onde estudantes de design trabalham, praticam e criam.
items.example_sentence_en: We work in the studio during class.
items.example_sentence_pt: Nós trabalhamos no estúdio durante a aula.
items.professional_context_en: The studio is a key place for Fashion Design learning and critique.
items.professional_context_pt: O estúdio é um lugar importante para aprendizagem e crítica em Design de Moda.
items.translation_notes_pt: Pode ser 'estúdio' ou 'ateliê', dependendo do contexto.
items.pronunciation_notes: Say STU-dee-oh with stress on the first syllable.

items.definition_en: A collection of work that shows a student's or designer's skills.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A group of projects, texts, or images that shows what you can do.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um conjunto de projetos, textos ou imagens que mostra o que você sabe fazer.
items.example_sentence_en: I want to write better texts for my portfolio.
items.example_sentence_pt: Eu quero escrever textos melhores para o meu portfólio.
items.professional_context_en: Portfolio language matters for presentations, internships, and future jobs.
items.professional_context_pt: A linguagem de portfólio é importante para apresentações, estágios e futuros trabalhos.
items.translation_notes_pt: A forma 'portfólio' é comum em cursos de moda.
items.pronunciation_notes: Say port-FOH-lee-oh with stress on FOH.

vocabulary_groups.title: First-semester coursework
vocabulary_groups.description: Words tied to the first-semester foundation courses named in the Week 1 manual.

items.definition_en: The activity of making images or lines by hand.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: Making a picture with lines and shapes.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Fazer uma imagem com linhas e formas.
items.example_sentence_en: I have drawing class this semester.
items.example_sentence_pt: Eu tenho aula de desenho neste semestre.
items.professional_context_en: Drawing is one of the first areas students mention in Fashion Design study.
items.professional_context_pt: Desenho é uma das primeiras áreas que os alunos mencionam em Design de Moda.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é 'desenho'.

items.definition_en: The activity of making or joining fabric with stitches.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: Working with fabric and stitches to make something.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Trabalhar com tecido e pontos para fazer alguma coisa.
items.example_sentence_en: I like sewing and fabric work.
items.example_sentence_pt: Eu gosto de costura e de trabalhar com tecido.
items.professional_context_en: Sewing vocabulary supports both studio practice and later process descriptions.
items.professional_context_pt: O vocabulário de costura ajuda tanto na prática de ateliê quanto em descrições de processo mais tarde.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução direta mais comum é 'costura'.
items.pronunciation_notes: Say SOH-ing. The w is silent.

items.definition_en: The process of creating pattern pieces for garments.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: Making the paper or shape pieces used to build a garment.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Criar as peças de papel ou de forma usadas para construir uma roupa.
items.example_sentence_en: Patternmaking is important for garment construction.
items.example_sentence_pt: Modelagem é importante para a construção da roupa.
items.professional_context_en: Students hear this word early in Fashion Design programs and reuse it later in Module 1.
items.professional_context_pt: Os alunos encontram essa palavra cedo no curso de Moda e a reutilizam depois no Módulo 1.
items.translation_notes_pt: Em contexto de moda, a tradução mais natural costuma ser 'modelagem'.
items.pronunciation_notes: Say PAT-ern-may-king with clear stress on PAT.

items.definition_en: The ability to produce original ideas.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: The ability to think of new and interesting ideas.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: A capacidade de pensar em ideias novas e interessantes.
items.example_sentence_en: Creativity is important in design work.
items.example_sentence_pt: Criatividade é importante no trabalho de design.
items.professional_context_en: The word connects English learning to idea generation and design process.
items.professional_context_pt: A palavra conecta o aprendizado de inglês à geração de ideias e ao processo de design.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução direta é 'criatividade'.
items.pronunciation_notes: Say kree-ay-TIV-i-tee with stress on TIV.

items.definition_en: The study of art from different periods and cultures.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: Learning about art from the past and from different places.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Estudar arte do passado e de lugares diferentes.
items.example_sentence_en: Art history helps students understand visual references.
items.example_sentence_pt: História da arte ajuda os alunos a entender referências visuais.
items.professional_context_en: Week 1 uses this term to show that English connects to broader design study, not only making clothes.
items.professional_context_pt: A Semana 1 usa esse termo para mostrar que o inglês se conecta ao estudo de design de forma ampla, não apenas a fazer roupas.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é 'história da arte'.
items.pronunciation_notes: Say art HIS-to-ree with stress on HIS.

items.definition_en: The work of planning and writing texts.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: Writing texts for class or projects.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Escrever textos para a aula ou para projetos.
items.example_sentence_en: Text production is useful for portfolio writing.
items.example_sentence_pt: Produção textual é útil para a escrita de portfólio.
items.professional_context_en: This term helps students connect English to academic and portfolio writing from the start.
items.professional_context_pt: Esse termo ajuda os alunos a conectar o inglês à escrita acadêmica e de portfólio desde o início.
items.translation_notes_pt: Pode ser aproximado por 'produção textual'.
items.pronunciation_notes: Stress pro-DUC-tion in the first word and TEXT in the phrase.

vocabulary_groups.title: Design objects and visual starters
vocabulary_groups.description: Visible design words students begin to describe and notice in Week 1.

items.definition_en: A quick drawing that shows a fashion idea.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A simple drawing of a clothing or design idea.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um desenho simples de uma ideia de roupa ou design.
items.example_sentence_en: This is my first sketch for class.
items.example_sentence_pt: Este é o meu primeiro croqui para a aula.
items.professional_context_en: Sketch is a key word for visual design work and later portfolio tasks.
items.professional_context_pt: Croqui é uma palavra importante para trabalho visual de design e para tarefas de portfólio depois.
items.translation_notes_pt: Em moda, pode ser 'croqui' ou 'esboço'.
items.pronunciation_notes: The final sound is short and clear: sketch.

items.definition_en: Material used to make clothing.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: The cloth used to make a garment.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: O tecido usado para fazer uma roupa.
items.example_sentence_en: I like working with fabric in sewing class.
items.example_sentence_pt: Eu gosto de trabalhar com tecido na aula de costura.
items.professional_context_en: Fabric vocabulary appears often in design descriptions and studio classes.
items.professional_context_pt: O vocabulário de tecido aparece com frequência em descrições de design e aulas de ateliê.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução direta mais comum é 'tecido'.

items.definition_en: A piece of clothing.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: One item of clothing.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Uma peça de roupa.
items.example_sentence_en: This garment is simple and clean.
items.example_sentence_pt: Esta peça de roupa é simples e limpa.
items.professional_context_en: The term helps students sound more professional than using only clothes or thing.
items.professional_context_pt: O termo ajuda os alunos a soar mais profissionais do que usando apenas clothes ou thing.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais próxima é 'peça de roupa'.
items.pronunciation_notes: Say GAR-ment with stress on GAR.

items.definition_en: An extra fashion item worn with clothing.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: An item like a bag, belt, or necklace that goes with a look.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um item como bolsa, cinto ou colar que acompanha um look.
items.example_sentence_en: She is interested in accessories.
items.example_sentence_pt: Ela tem interesse em acessórios.
items.professional_context_en: The term supports early conversation about design interests and future course areas.
items.professional_context_pt: O termo ajuda em conversas iniciais sobre interesses de design e areas futuras do curso.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução direta é 'acessório'.
items.pronunciation_notes: Say ak-SES-uh-ree with stress on SES.

items.definition_en: A group of fashion pieces designed together.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A set of fashion items that belong together.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um conjunto de itens de moda que pertencem ao mesmo grupo.
items.example_sentence_en: This is my first collection idea.
items.example_sentence_pt: Esta é a minha primeira ideia de coleção.
items.professional_context_en: Collection is useful when students start talking about design direction and future projects.
items.professional_context_pt: Coleção é útil quando os alunos começam a falar sobre direção de design e projetos futuros.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é 'coleção'.
items.pronunciation_notes: Say kuh-LEK-shun with stress on LEK.

vocabulary_groups.title: Goals, preferences, and support phrases
vocabulary_groups.description: Simple phrases students need for profile writing, speaking, and early feedback routines.

items.definition_en: A phrase used to name an area you want to know more about.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A phrase for saying what area or topic attracts you.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Uma expressão para dizer qual área ou tema chama sua atenção.
items.example_sentence_en: I am interested in sustainable fashion.
items.example_sentence_pt: Eu tenho interesse em moda sustentável.
items.professional_context_en: Students use this phrase to sound more specific when naming design interests.
items.professional_context_pt: Os alunos usam essa expressão para soar mais específicos ao nomear interesses de design.

weeks.lesson_plan_markdown:
# Week 1: Welcome to Fashion Design English

## Overview
Week 1 establishes the routine for the whole course and should feel welcoming, visual, and clearly tied to Fashion Design study. Students learn how the weekly cycle works, complete a light diagnostic, read and listen to simple model introductions, practice starter vocabulary, write a short profile, and review one corrected sentence before a teacher-led speaking session.

This gold-standard Week 1 is still accessible for mixed A2-B1 learners, but it is complete enough to show how future weeks should combine app-ready structure, bilingual student support, professional relevance, assessment guidance, and asset planning.

## Learning Objectives
- Identify the main parts of the weekly course routine.
- Recognize and use starter Fashion Design and course-routine vocabulary.
- Understand the main ideas and key details in one short reading and one short listening text.
- Write a 50-80 word student profile using guided sentence frames.
- Revise one sentence after correction feedback.
- Deliver a short oral introduction with teacher support.

## Professional Fashion-Design Context
The week connects English to first-semester Fashion Design coursework from the beginning. Students meet vocabulary linked to drawing, sewing, patternmaking, creativity, text production, studio work, and portfolio building. The language is not generic self-introduction practice. It is the language students need to explain who they are as design students, what they study, what kinds of fashion work interest them, and why English matters for class tasks and future professional communication.

## Language Objectives
- Use beginner-accessible identity frames such as "My name is ___," "I am a fashion design student," "I study ___," and "I want to learn English for ___."
- Recognize and use core terms such as fashion design, sketch, fabric, garment, sewing, patternmaking, studio, portfolio, feedback, and submit.
- Use simple preference and goal language such as "I like ___," "I am interested in ___," and "English can help me with ___."
- Notice common correction targets, especially missing articles, missing verbs, and verb patterns after like and want.

## Materials Needed
- One welcome visual or slide for the weekly routine.
- One reading-support image for the Ana profile.
- One short listening audio clip or teacher read-aloud script.
- A small image set for Week 1 vocabulary practice.
- Student writing space for a 50-80 word profile.
- Teacher pronunciation list for the live session.

## Suggested Sequence
1. `m01w01-a01` Start Here: students meet the weekly rhythm and complete a light diagnostic about interests and goals.
2. `m01w01-a02` Meet Ana: students read a short model profile and answer gist/detail questions.
3. `m01w01-a03` Listen: students hear a first-semester student introduction and identify classes, interests, and English goals.
4. `m01w01-a04` Vocabulary Starter: students connect words to visuals, Portuguese support, and sentence frames.
5. `m01w01-a05` Fashion Student Profile: students write a short reusable profile in English.
6. `m01w01-a06` Review and Improve: students focus on one corrected sentence and save a revision.
7. `m01w01-a07` Teacher Session: students practice pronunciation, give a short spoken introduction, and confirm that they understand the course routine.

## Timing Estimate
- `m01w01-a01` 10 minutes
- `m01w01-a02` 12 minutes
- `m01w01-a03` 12 minutes
- `m01w01-a04` 15 minutes
- `m01w01-a05` 20 minutes
- `m01w01-a06` 8 minutes
- `m01w01-a07` 50 minutes

Total planned time: 127 minutes.

The asynchronous/app-style portion is 77 minutes. The teacher-led speaking session is 50 minutes.

## Differentiation Options
- Let learners who need more support keep the English sentence frames visible during reading, listening, writing, and speaking.
- Provide a reduced writing path with four required sentences before inviting one optional challenge sentence.
- Offer a visible word bank during listening for students who need extra comprehension support.
- Allow oral rehearsal in pairs before students write or speak in the teacher-led session.
- Challenge stronger learners to add one sentence about a specific design area such as sustainability, accessories, styling, or portfolio goals.

## Extension Options
- Ask students to add one sentence describing a favorite design object such as a sketch, garment, fabric, or accessory.
- Invite students to compare their profile with Ana's model profile and identify one similarity and one difference.
- During the live session, ask confident learners to respond to one follow-up question such as "What is your favorite area in fashion design?" or "Why do you want English for portfolio work?"

## Notes for Future App Implementation
Week 1 maps well to a clear onboarding flow with an orientation card, reading card, listening player, image-supported vocabulary practice, text-entry writing task, correction review card, and teacher-reviewed speaking checkpoint.

The future app should preserve:
- bilingual English and Brazilian Portuguese student-facing text
- visible sentence frames and success criteria
- teacher visibility into the profile draft and revision step
- audio fallback with transcript release after attempt
- teacher-session support notes, not just app-graded tasks

The vocabulary image set should be reusable in later weeks, especially for studio tools, garments, and visual-description tasks.
weeks.teacher_notes_markdown:
# Teacher Notes: Week 1 - Welcome to Fashion Design English

## Common Learner Difficulties
Students may omit the verb in "I am," forget the article in "a fashion design student," or use Portuguese word order in short English sentences. Many learners will also confuse course areas and design objects, for example using sketch, drawing, garment, and fabric interchangeably. In listening, they may recognize isolated words but miss the speaker's overall goal. In writing, students may produce very general statements unless the teacher keeps the Fashion Design context visible.

## Classroom Management Suggestions
Keep Week 1 low-pressure and welcoming. Model each task briefly before students work independently. During the teacher-led session, allow students to read from their written profile first, then encourage more natural delivery on a second try. Use quick checks rather than long explanations, especially during pronunciation work and profile sharing.

## Professional Context Notes
Students should leave Week 1 understanding that English is a practical tool for Fashion Design study, not a separate abstract subject. Refer often to real first-semester work such as drawing classes, sewing, patternmaking, creativity lab, text production, studio routines, and early portfolio writing. When students name their interests, invite answers that sound realistic for a design student rather than generic hobbies.

## Cultural or Industry Notes
Some students may already know fashion vocabulary from media, trends, or brand culture, but they may not yet know how to use those words in an academic or studio setting. Keep examples adult and professionally grounded. Avoid making Week 1 feel childish just because the language level is controlled.

## Simplify This Week
Reduce the profile task to four required sentences if needed:
- My name is ___.
- I am a fashion design student.
- I like ___.
- I want to learn English for ___.

If the listening task feels too demanding, read the script aloud slowly, pause between ideas, and allow students to check a keyword list before the second listen.

## Extend This Week
Ask stronger learners to add a sentence about a future design interest such as sustainability, accessories, styling, or fashion research. In the teacher-led session, they can also answer a follow-up question and give one simple feedback phrase to a classmate, such as "I like your idea about sketches" or "You can add one more detail."

## Asynchronous or App-Based Adaptation
In a future app, the reading, listening, and vocabulary activities can be auto-checked, while the writing task should remain teacher-visible with light rubric guidance. The correction-review task should save the revised sentence so teachers can see whether the learner acted on feedback. The teacher-led session should remain represented in the canonical week content even if it is not app-graded, because it is where pronunciation, confidence, and live support are reinforced.

steps.teacher_action: Encourage students to use the image as evidence.

steps.title: Answer the image questions
steps.student_action_en: Choose the best answer about what each object is and where it is.
steps.student_action_pt: Escolha a melhor resposta sobre o que cada objeto é e onde ele está.
steps.teacher_action: Guide students back to phrases such as on the table and near the sewing machine.

steps.title: Check key phrases
steps.student_action_en: Review one or two correct location phrases after you answer.
steps.student_action_pt: Revise uma ou duas expressões corretas de localização depois de responder.
steps.teacher_action: Preview how these phrases support the writing task.

expected_output.description_en: Five to seven selected answers about object identity and location in the studio scene.
expected_output.description_pt: De cinco a sete respostas selecionadas sobre identidade e localização de objetos na cena do estúdio.

completion_criteria_en: The student identifies key objects in the image.
The student understands at least one basic location phrase.
The student answers with image-based evidence.
completion_criteria_pt: O aluno identifica objetos importantes na imagem.
O aluno entende pelo menos uma expressão básica de localização.
O aluno responde com base em evidências da imagem.
checklist_en: I looked closely at the image.
I answered the object questions.
I used location phrases from the picture.
checklist_pt: Eu observei a imagem com atenção.
Eu respondi às perguntas sobre os objetos.
Eu usei expressões de localização da imagem.
assessment.model_response_en: The ruler is on the table. The thread is near the sewing machine. The body-shaped form is a mannequin.
assessment.model_response_pt: A régua está sobre a mesa. A linha está perto da máquina de costura. A forma em formato de corpo é um manequim.
common_errors: Choosing answers without checking the image carefully.
Mixing up near and on the table.
feedback_prompts_en: Point to the object in the image. What do you see next to it or under it?
feedback_prompts_pt: Aponte para o objeto na imagem. O que você vê ao lado dele ou embaixo dele?

support: Allow students to review the vocabulary boards before answering the image questions.
challenge: Ask stronger learners to say one full sentence with on the table or near the sewing machine.

extension_options: Write one more location sentence about a visible object in the scene.
activities.notes_for_app_design: Render this as one large reusable studio-scene image with six short app-checked questions below it. Keep the interaction to quick taps and choices rather than typing. The app should surface location-language feedback after submission.

activities.title: Listen: Studio Instructions
activities.summary: Students listen to short studio instructions and identify tools, actions, and a simple order of steps.

en.title: Listen: Studio Instructions
en.summary: Listen to the studio instructions and choose the correct tools and actions.
en.instructions: Listen once for the main idea. Listen again for details about the tools, actions, and order.
success_criteria: I can understand the main studio task.
I can hear some important tools and actions.
I can follow a short sequence of simple instructions.

pt.title: Escute: instruções do estúdio
pt.summary: Escute as instruções do estúdio e escolha as ferramentas e ações corretas.
pt.instructions: Escute uma vez para entender a ideia principal. Escute novamente para os detalhes sobre ferramentas, ações e ordem.
success_criteria: Eu consigo entender a tarefa principal do estúdio.
Eu consigo ouvir algumas ferramentas e ações importantes.
Eu consigo acompanhar uma sequência curta de instruções simples.

activities.teacher_instructions: Play the audio two or three times maximum. Keep the first listen focused on gist and reveal the transcript only after the attempt.
materials: audio player or teacher read-aloud script

input.prompt_en: Listen to the studio instructions and answer the questions.
input.prompt_pt: Escute as instruções do estúdio e responda às perguntas.

items.label_en: What is the main place in the audio?
items.label_pt: Qual é o lugar principal no áudio?

items.label_en: Which objects should students take first?
items.label_pt: Quais objetos os alunos devem pegar primeiro?

items.label_en: The teacher says to sew immediately.
items.label_pt: O professor diz para costurar imediatamente.

items.label_en: What do students put on the table?
items.label_pt: O que os alunos colocam sobre a mesa?

items.label_en: Which action comes before pin the fabric?
items.label_pt: Qual ação acontece antes de prender o tecido com alfinetes?

steps.title: Listen for the main task
steps.student_action_en: Listen once and decide where the students are and what kind of task they are doing.
steps.student_action_pt: Escute uma vez e decida onde os alunos estão e que tipo de tarefa estão fazendo.
steps.teacher_action: Tell students not to worry about every word in the first listen.

steps.title: Listen for tools and actions
steps.student_action_en: Listen again and choose the tools, actions, and details you hear.
steps.student_action_pt: Escute novamente e escolha as ferramentas, ações e detalhes que você ouve.
steps.teacher_action: Let students replay the audio up to two more times if needed.

steps.title: Check one sequence detail
steps.student_action_en: Notice which action comes before the next one.
steps.student_action_pt: Perceba qual ação acontece antes da próxima.
steps.teacher_action: Show the transcript only after students answer.

expected_output.description_en: Main-idea and detail selections about studio instructions, including one simple sequence check.
expected_output.description_pt: Seleções de ideia principal e detalhes sobre instruções do estúdio, incluindo uma verificação simples de sequência.

completion_criteria_en: The student identifies the studio context.
The student recognizes key tools and actions from the audio.
The student follows at least one simple order relationship.
completion_criteria_pt: O aluno identifica o contexto do estúdio.
O aluno reconhece ferramentas e ações importantes no áudio.
O aluno acompanha pelo menos uma relação simples de ordem.
checklist_en: I listened for the main idea.
I listened again for details.
I checked the order of one action.
checklist_pt: Eu escutei para entender a ideia principal.
Eu escutei novamente para os detalhes.
Eu conferi a ordem de uma ação.
assessment.model_response_en: Students are in the fashion studio. They take the sketchbook, pencil, ruler, and measuring tape, put the fabric on the table, and fold the fabric before they use pins.
assessment.model_response_pt: Os alunos estão no estúdio de moda. Eles pegam o caderno de croquis, o lápis, a régua e a fita métrica, colocam o tecido sobre a mesa e dobram o tecido antes de usar alfinetes.
common_errors: Choosing an object that sounds familiar but is not in the audio.
Missing the negative instruction Do not sew yet.
feedback_prompts_en: Listen again for the verbs. What do students do first, next, and later?
feedback_prompts_pt: Escute novamente os verbos. O que os alunos fazem primeiro, depois e mais tarde?

support: Show a small visual word bank of the key tools before the second listen.
challenge: Ask stronger learners to repeat one instruction aloud after the final listen.

extension_options: Write or say one more simple instruction using Week 2 words.
activities.notes_for_app_design: Render this as an audio player with replay support and five short objective questions underneath. Allow two or three plays. Keep transcript reveal behind the first attempt. Auto-check the responses and show which tools and verbs were important.

activities.title: Tool + Action Phrase Practice
activities.activity_type_custom: Tool-action phrase practice for controlled studio-purpose language.
activities.summary: Students connect tools to actions by completing short I use ___ to ___ phrases with strong A2 support.

en.title: Tool + Action Phrase Practice
en.summary: Complete the short phrases about tools and actions in the studio.
en.instructions: Use the word bank to complete each sentence. Focus on the pattern I use ___ to ___.
success_criteria: I can connect a tool to a simple action.
I can use the pattern I use ___ to ___.
I can build short studio-purpose phrases.

pt.title: Prática de frases: ferramenta + ação
pt.summary: Complete as frases curtas sobre ferramentas e ações no estúdio.
pt.instructions: Use o banco de palavras para completar cada frase. Foque no padrão I use ___ to ___.
success_criteria: Eu consigo conectar uma ferramenta a uma ação simples.
Eu consigo usar o padrão I use ___ to ___.
Eu consigo construir frases curtas de finalidade no estúdio.

activities.teacher_instructions: Keep the task controlled and fast. This is not free writing. The goal is accurate phrase-building that prepares students for the Week 2 writing task.

input.prompt_en: Complete the tool-and-action phrases.
input.prompt_pt: Complete as frases de ferramenta e ação.

items.label_pt: Complete a frase sobre cortar.
Complete a frase sobre desenhar.
items.sentence_frame_en: I use a ___ to draw lines.
items.sentence_frame_pt: I use a ___ to draw lines.

items.label_pt: Complete a frase sobre medir.
Complete a frase sobre prender com alfinetes.
Complete a frase sobre costurar.

steps.title: Notice the pattern
steps.student_action_en: Look at the model pattern I use ___ to ___.
steps.student_action_pt: Observe o modelo I use ___ to ___.
steps.teacher_action: Model one example aloud before students complete the set.

steps.title: Complete the phrases
steps.student_action_en: Choose the correct tool from the word bank for each action.
steps.student_action_pt: Escolha a ferramenta correta do banco de palavras para cada ação.
steps.teacher_action: Remind students to notice articles with singular tools.

steps.title: Say one phrase
steps.student_action_en: Read one completed phrase aloud or quietly to yourself.
steps.student_action_pt: Leia uma frase completa em voz alta ou em voz baixa para você mesmo.
steps.teacher_action: Use this as a bridge into the writing task.

expected_output.description_en: Five to six completed I use ___ to ___ phrases.
expected_output.description_pt: De cinco a seis frases completas com o padrão I use ___ to ___.

completion_criteria_en: The student uses the target phrase pattern correctly.
The student matches tools to logical actions.
The student completes the set with short accurate answers.
completion_criteria_pt: O aluno usa corretamente o padrão de frase-alvo.
O aluno relaciona ferramentas a ações lógicas.
O aluno completa o conjunto com respostas curtas e corretas.
checklist_en: I used the sentence pattern.
I matched the tools and actions.
I am ready to use these phrases in writing.
checklist_pt: Eu usei o padrão da frase.
Eu relacionei as ferramentas e as ações.
Eu estou pronto para usar essas frases na escrita.
assessment.model_response_en: I use scissors to cut fabric. I use a ruler to draw lines. I use a measuring tape to measure. I use pins to hold fabric. I use a sewing machine to sew.
assessment.model_response_pt: Eu uso tesoura para cortar tecido. Eu uso uma régua para desenhar linhas. Eu uso uma fita métrica para medir. Eu uso alfinetes para prender o tecido. Eu uso uma máquina de costura para costurar.
common_errors: Leaving out to in the purpose phrase.
Using a singular tool without an article.
Choosing a tool that does not match the action.
feedback_prompts_en: Check the pattern again. Do you have I use plus object plus to plus verb?
feedback_prompts_pt: Confira o padrão novamente. Você tem I use mais objeto mais to mais verbo?

support: Show a smaller word bank with only two choices per item.
challenge: Ask stronger learners to add one extra phrase without a word bank.

extension_options: Write one new phrase with a tool that is not in the activity set.
activities.notes_for_app_design: Render this as a controlled fill-blank set with visible word banks. Save the completed phrase set as objective output. Auto-check each blank and highlight the purpose pattern I use ___ to ___. If visual support is helpful, a future app may reuse the Week 2 vocabulary boards instead of requiring a dedicated new asset.

activities.title: My Studio Kit
activities.summary: Students build a short structured text about the tools and materials they use in the studio by completing sentence frames.

en.title: My Studio Kit
en.summary: Build a short text about your studio kit with sentence frames.
en.instructions: Complete the sentence frames about the tools and materials you have and use. Save your answers as one short studio-kit text.
success_criteria: I can complete 4-5 sentence frames about my studio kit.
I can use Week 2 tool words in a short text.
I can submit a clear studio-kit description for teacher feedback.
sentence_frames: In my studio kit, I have ___.

pt.title: Meu kit de estúdio
pt.summary: Monte um texto curto sobre o seu kit de estúdio com frases-modelo.
pt.instructions: Complete as frases-modelo sobre as ferramentas e os materiais que você tem e usa. Salve as respostas como um texto curto sobre o seu kit de estúdio.
success_criteria: Eu consigo completar de 4 a 5 frases-modelo sobre o meu kit de estúdio.
Eu consigo usar palavras da Semana 2 em um texto curto.
Eu consigo enviar uma descrição clara do meu kit de estúdio para feedback do professor.
sentence_frames: In my studio kit, I have ___.

activities.teacher_instructions: Treat this as the meaningful written output for Week 2. Keep the base requirement limited to 4-6 completed sentence frames. Focus feedback on task completion, accurate tool vocabulary, article use, plural forms, and the pattern I use ___ to ___. Allow one revision if needed.

input.prompt_en: Complete 4 to 6 sentence frames about your studio kit.
input.prompt_pt: Complete de 4 a 6 frases-modelo sobre o seu kit de estúdio.

items.label_pt: Frase-modelo 1
items.sentence_frame_en: In my studio kit, I have ___.
items.sentence_frame_pt: In my studio kit, I have ___.

items.label_pt: Frase-modelo 2
Frase-modelo 3
Frase-modelo 4
Frase opcional de desafio

steps.title: Review the sentence frames
steps.student_action_en: Read the sentence frames and choose the tools and actions you want to use.
steps.student_action_pt: Leia as frases-modelo e escolha as ferramentas e ações que você quer usar.
steps.teacher_action: Remind students that the base task is short and structured, not a full paragraph.

steps.title: Build your studio-kit text
steps.student_action_en: Complete 4 to 6 sentence frames and save them as one short text.
steps.student_action_pt: Complete de 4 a 6 frases-modelo e salve-as como um texto curto.
steps.teacher_action: Monitor article use, plural forms, and the phrase I use ___ to ___.

steps.title: Check before you submit
steps.student_action_en: Read your text once and check whether each sentence is clear.
steps.student_action_pt: Leia o seu texto uma vez e confira se cada frase está clara.
steps.teacher_action: Encourage a simple self-check before teacher review.

expected_output.description_en: A short saved studio-kit text built from 4 to 5 sentence-frame completions, with one extra sentence only as an optional challenge.
expected_output.description_pt: Um texto curto salvo sobre o kit de estúdio, construído a partir de 4 a 5 frases-modelo completadas, com uma frase extra apenas como desafio opcional.
expected_output.length_or_format: 4 to 5 short sentences saved as one text, with 1 optional challenge sentence

completion_criteria_en: The student completes at least four sentence frames.
The text names real Week 2 tools or materials.
The text includes at least one clear tool-and-purpose phrase.
completion_criteria_pt: O aluno completa pelo menos quatro frases-modelo.
O texto nomeia ferramentas ou materiais reais da Semana 2.
O texto inclui pelo menos uma frase clara de ferramenta e finalidade.
checklist_en: I completed 4 to 5 sentence frames.
I used Week 2 tool words.
I checked my text before I submitted it.
checklist_pt: Eu completei de 4 a 5 frases-modelo.
Eu usei palavras de ferramentas da Semana 2.
Eu revisei o meu texto antes de enviar.

rubric.excellent_en: The text completes the required frames and includes clear tool, purpose, and need information.
rubric.excellent_pt: O texto completa as frases obrigatórias e inclui informações claras sobre ferramenta, finalidade e necessidade.
rubric.satisfactory_en: The text completes most required frames and is mostly clear.
rubric.satisfactory_pt: O texto completa a maior parte das frases obrigatórias e está razoavelmente claro.
rubric.needs_work_en: The text is missing required frames or is too incomplete to understand clearly.
rubric.needs_work_pt: O texto não completa as frases obrigatórias ou está incompleto demais para ser entendido com clareza.

rubric.excellent_en: The text uses I use ___ to ___ and article or plural forms accurately most of the time.
rubric.excellent_pt: O texto usa I use ___ to ___ e formas de artigo ou plural corretamente na maior parte do tempo.
rubric.satisfactory_en: The text uses the target phrases with minor mistakes that do not block meaning.
rubric.satisfactory_pt: O texto usa as frases-alvo com pequenos erros que não impedem a compreensão.
rubric.needs_work_en: The text needs support with the target phrase pattern, articles, or plurals.
rubric.needs_work_pt: O texto precisa de apoio com o padrão das frases-alvo, artigos ou plurais.

assessment.model_response_en: In my studio kit, I have scissors, a ruler, a measuring tape, and a sketchbook. I use scissors to cut fabric. I need pattern paper for class. My favorite tool is my sketchbook. It is useful because I draw ideas in it.
assessment.model_response_pt: No meu kit de estúdio, eu tenho tesoura, uma régua, uma fita métrica e um caderno de croquis. Eu uso tesoura para cortar tecido. Eu preciso de papel de modelagem para a aula. A minha ferramenta favorita é o meu caderno de croquis. Ele é útil porque eu desenho ideias nele.
common_errors: Missing articles in a ruler or a pencil.
Using a singular form with scissors.
Writing I use scissors cut fabric without to.
Leaving the text too short to show the required elements.
feedback_prompts_en: Add one clearer tool word from Week 2.
Check your article or plural form.
Please revise one sentence with I use ___ to ___.
feedback_prompts_pt: Acrescente uma palavra de ferramenta da Semana 2 com mais clareza.
Confira o seu artigo ou a sua forma no plural.
Por favor, revise uma frase com o padrão I use ___ to ___.

support: Allow students to complete exactly four core frames with a visible word bank.
challenge: Invite stronger learners to add one extra sentence about location or usefulness.

extension_options: Turn one sentence from the text into a spoken sentence for the teacher session.
activities.notes_for_app_design: Render this as a teacher-reviewed structured writing submission with separate sentence-frame fields that are saved as one short text. Keep the base task to 4 to 5 required sentence-frame completions and show any extra sentence as an optional challenge only. The teacher view should show the completed frames, the required-elements checklist, common error prompts, quick feedback tags, and a return-for-revision option. Do not require long free writing.

activities.title: Review and Improve: Articles and Plurals
activities.summary: Students review one common Week 2 sentence problem and save one corrected version.

en.title: Review and Improve: Articles and Plurals
en.summary: Study one correction card and write the improved sentence.
en.instructions: Choose one correction card, notice the mistake, and write the corrected sentence clearly.
success_criteria: I can notice one common sentence problem.
I can write one corrected sentence clearly.
I can use the correction to improve my own writing.
sentence_frames: I use a ruler to draw a line.
I use scissors to cut fabric.
My favorite tool is my sketchbook.

pt.title: Revise e melhore: artigos e plurais
pt.summary: Observe um cartão de correção e escreva a frase melhorada.
pt.instructions: Escolha um cartão de correção, observe o erro e escreva a frase corrigida com clareza.
success_criteria: Eu consigo perceber um problema comum em uma frase.
Eu consigo escrever uma frase corrigida com clareza.
Eu consigo usar a correção para melhorar a minha própria escrita.
sentence_frames: I use a ruler to draw a line.
I use scissors to cut fabric.
My favorite tool is my sketchbook.

activities.teacher_instructions: Keep the revision target small and specific. Connect the correction back to the Week 2 writing task so students can transfer it immediately.

input.prompt_en: Choose one Week 2 sentence and write the corrected version.
input.prompt_pt: Escolha uma frase da Semana 2 e escreva a versão corrigida.

items.label_pt: Corrija o problema de artigo.
items.incorrect_sentence: I use ruler to draw line.
items.correct_sentence: I use a ruler to draw a line.
accepted_answers: I use a ruler to draw a line.

items.label_pt: Corrija a forma no plural.
items.incorrect_sentence: I use scissor to cut fabric.
items.correct_sentence: I use scissors to cut fabric.
accepted_answers: I use scissors to cut fabric.

items.label_pt: Corrija a falta de to.
items.correct_sentence: I use pins to hold fabric.
accepted_answers: I use pins to hold fabric.

steps.title: Choose a correction card
steps.student_action_en: Read one incorrect sentence and the correction focus.
steps.student_action_pt: Leia uma frase incorreta e o foco da correção.
steps.teacher_action: Name the three main Week 2 correction targets: articles, plurals, and to plus verb.

steps.title: Write the corrected sentence
steps.student_action_en: Rewrite the sentence clearly and accurately.
steps.student_action_pt: Reescreva a frase com clareza e precisão.
steps.teacher_action: Ask students to compare the corrected model with their own writing.

steps.title: Transfer the correction
steps.student_action_en: Check if the same problem appears in your studio-kit text.
steps.student_action_pt: Confira se o mesmo problema aparece no seu texto sobre o kit de estúdio.
steps.teacher_action: Prompt students to fix their own sentence if needed.

expected_output.description_en: One corrected Week 2 sentence saved after review.
expected_output.description_pt: Uma frase corrigida da Semana 2 salva após a revisão.

completion_criteria_en: The student chooses one correction card.
The student writes the corrected sentence accurately.
The student checks for transfer into personal writing.
completion_criteria_pt: O aluno escolhe um cartão de correção.
O aluno escreve a frase corrigida corretamente.
O aluno verifica a possibilidade de transferir a correção para a própria escrita.
checklist_en: I chose one correction card.
I wrote the corrected sentence.
I checked my own text for the same problem.
checklist_pt: Eu escolhi um cartão de correção.
Eu escrevi a frase corrigida.
Eu verifiquei o meu próprio texto para o mesmo problema.
assessment.model_response_en: I use a ruler to draw a line.
assessment.model_response_pt: Eu uso uma régua para desenhar uma linha.
common_errors: Keeping the original mistake in the new sentence.
Fixing one part but forgetting another missing word.
feedback_prompts_en: Read the corrected model again. Which word was missing?
feedback_prompts_pt: Leia o modelo corrigido novamente. Qual palavra estava faltando?

support: Limit the choice to two correction cards for students who need more support.
challenge: Ask stronger learners to explain the correction rule in simple English or Portuguese.

extension_options: Correct one more sentence from your own Week 2 writing.
activities.notes_for_app_design: Render this as one correction-card activity with a small set of common Week 2 sentence problems. Let the student choose one card, type or select the corrected version, and compare against accepted answers. Save one corrected sentence as the mini-revision artifact.

activities.title: Teacher Session: Show Your Studio Kit
activities.summary: Students use Week 2 writing and sentence frames to say what tools they have and what they use them for in a live teacher-supported session.

en.title: Teacher Session: Show Your Studio Kit
en.summary: Use your Week 2 writing to name your tools and say what they are for.
en.instructions: Bring your Week 2 text, practice the key tool words, and say 4 to 6 short sentences about your studio kit.
success_criteria: I can name several studio tools clearly.
I can say what I use a tool for.
I can speak in short sentences with teacher support.
sentence_frames: In my studio kit, I have ___.

pt.title: Sessão com o professor: mostre o seu kit de estúdio
pt.summary: Use a sua escrita da Semana 2 para nomear as suas ferramentas e dizer para que elas servem.

success_criteria: Eu consigo nomear várias ferramentas do estúdio com clareza.

sentence_frames: In my studio kit, I have ___.

activities.teacher_instructions: Use the live session to move the Week 2 language from recognition and writing into supported speaking. Keep the task short and concrete. input.prompt_en: Use your Week 2 studio-kit text to speak about your tools and what they are for.
input.prompt_pt: Use o seu texto da Semana 2 sobre o kit de estúdio para falar sobre as suas ferramentas e para que elas servem.

items.label_en: Say 4 to 6 short sentences about the tools in your studio kit.
items.label_pt: Diga de 4 a 6 frases curtas sobre as ferramentas do seu kit de estúdio.

items.label_en: Include at least one sentence with I use ___ to ___.
items.label_pt: Inclua pelo menos uma frase com I use ___ to ___.

steps.student_action_pt: Pratique palavras importantes da Semana 2 como scissors, ruler, measuring tape, sewing machine, sketchbook e mannequin.

steps.title: Show your studio kit

steps.student_action_pt: Use o seu texto da Semana 2 para dizer de 4 a 6 frases sobre as ferramentas que você tem e para que você as usa.

weeks.lesson_plan_markdown:
# Week 2: The Fashion Studio

## Overview
Week 2 introduces the fashion studio as the student’s first practical English environment inside Fashion Design study. The week stays highly visual and A2-accessible. Students begin with a studio-scene review, learn core tool and material vocabulary, read a detailed image, listen to simple instructions, practice tool-and-purpose phrases, write a short structured studio-kit text, and review one sentence correction before a teacher-led speaking session.

Week 2 follows the same general rhythm as Week 1, but it shifts the content from identity language to concrete objects, places, and actions. The priority is recognition before production, then short controlled production before live speaking.

## Learning Objectives
- Recognize and name common Fashion Design studio tools, materials, and work areas.
- Understand short A2-level studio instructions with simple classroom actions.
- Identify objects and location phrases in a visual studio scene.
- Use sentence frames such as `This is ___`, `These are ___`, `I use ___ to ___`, and `I need ___`.
- Write a short 4-5 sentence studio-kit text with strong support, with one extra sentence only as an optional challenge.
- Revise one sentence focused on articles, plurals, or missing `to`.
- Say 4-6 short sentences about tools and purposes during the teacher session.

## Professional Fashion-Design Context
This week is closely tied to introductory sewing, patternmaking, observation drawing, and creativity lab routines. Students need English not only for abstract study goals but also for everyday classroom actions: taking a sketchbook, measuring fabric, finding tools on the table, and naming what they use in the studio. The tasks reflect the language of materials, surfaces, tools, and teacher instructions rather than generic ESL vocabulary.

## Language Objectives
- Name common objects such as `scissors`, `ruler`, `measuring tape`, `needle`, `thread`, `pins`, `sewing machine`, `mannequin`, `sketchbook`, `pattern paper`, and `fabric swatch`.
- Understand and use short imperative verbs such as `take`, `put`, `draw`, `cut`, `measure`, `fold`, and `pin`.
- Use singular and plural object phrases more accurately, especially `a ruler`, `a pencil`, `scissors`, and `pins`.
- Connect object and purpose with `I use ___ to ___`.
- Build a short text from sentence frames instead of writing a broad paragraph from scratch.

## Materials Needed
- One full studio or worktable scene for the opener and visual-reading task.
- One visual vocabulary board or small set of isolated tool and material images.
- One short studio-instructions audio clip or teacher read-aloud fallback.
- Sentence frames for `I use ___ to ___`, `I need ___`, and `My favorite tool is ___`.
- Student writing space for the Week 2 studio-kit text.
- Optional printed image cards for the teacher-led naming and speaking session.

## Suggested Sequence
1. `m01w02-a01` Welcome Back: students review familiar words and notice a studio scene.
2. `m01w02-a02` Studio Vocabulary: students match images, words, and Portuguese support for tools and materials.
3. `m01w02-a03` Look Around the Studio: students answer object and location questions from a detailed image.
4. `m01w02-a04` Listen: Studio Instructions: students hear short teacher directions and choose tools, actions, and order.
5. `m01w02-a05` Tool + Action Phrase Practice: students complete `I use ___ to ___` phrases.
6. `m01w02-a06` My Studio Kit: students build a short structured text from sentence frames.
7. `m01w02-a07` Review and Improve: students correct one sentence with an article, plural, or infinitive problem.
8. `m01w02-a08` Teacher Session: students name studio items and explain what they use them for in live speaking.

## Timing Estimate
- `m01w02-a01` 6 minutes
- `m01w02-a02` 14 minutes
- `m01w02-a03` 12 minutes
- `m01w02-a04` 12 minutes
- `m01w02-a05` 10 minutes
- `m01w02-a06` 18 minutes
- `m01w02-a07` 7 minutes
- `m01w02-a08` 50 minutes

Total planned time: 129 minutes.

The asynchronous or app-style portion is 79 minutes. The teacher-led speaking session is 50 minutes.

## Differentiation Options
- Keep image support visible during vocabulary, listening, and writing.
- Let learners who need more support choose from a reduced word bank before typing sentence frames.
- Provide a model tool-and-action phrase beside the writing task for students who need stronger scaffolding.
- Allow pair rehearsal before the teacher-observed speaking task.
- Ask stronger learners to add one extra sentence about location or usefulness, such as `The fabric is on the table` or `My sketchbook is useful because I draw ideas in class`.

## Extension Options
- Invite stronger learners to sort tools into drawing, measuring, and sewing categories using English labels.
- Ask students to add one more sentence comparing two tools, for example `I use a pencil to draw, but I use pins to hold fabric`.
- During the teacher session, ask confident learners one follow-up question such as `Where is your measuring tape?` or `Why is your sketchbook useful?`

## Notes for Future App Implementation
Week 2 maps cleanly to a visual-first mobile flow. The app-facing design should preserve:

- a reusable studio-scene image that supports both recognition and location tasks
- image-word matching with Portuguese support hidden behind the target English focus
- audio replay for the studio-instructions task with transcript reveal only after an attempt
- sentence-frame writing fields rather than one large blank text box
- a teacher-visible structured writing submission with revision support for the studio-kit task
- a teacher-observed speaking checkpoint that tracks completion without recording audio

The week is especially reusable because the vocabulary boards and the `I use ___ to ___` pattern will return in later modules.
weeks.teacher_notes_markdown:
# Teacher Notes: Week 2 - The Fashion Studio

## Common Learner Difficulties
Students may confuse similar tools such as ruler and measuring tape, or thread and fabric. They may omit articles in singular phrases like `I use ruler` or `I have pencil`. They may also overgeneralize plurals, for example `a scissors`, or produce incomplete purpose phrases such as `I use scissors cut fabric`. In listening, learners may identify familiar objects but miss the order of instructions.

## Classroom Management Suggestions
Keep the week highly visual and concrete. Show the image before explaining too much language. Model one item or one phrase first, then let students complete the rest. During the teacher session, allow students to look at their Week 2 writing while they speak. Keep the correction step narrow so students act on one clear grammar point rather than trying to fix everything at once.

## Professional Context Notes
Use real Fashion Design routines and avoid generic school-only examples. Point back to drawing, sewing, patternmaking, and classroom studio organization. When students say what they use, encourage answers that sound like real studio practice: `I use a measuring tape to measure`, `I use pins to hold fabric`, and `I use a sketchbook to draw ideas`.

## Cultural or Industry Notes
Some terms may overlap with words students already know from Portuguese or from informal fashion media, but the classroom goal is accurate English use in a studio-learning context. Keep the tone adult and practical. A2 language should still sound connected to university study and future professional work.

## Simplify This Week
Reduce the writing task to four required frames only:
- In my studio kit, I have ___.
- I use ___ to ___.
- I need ___ for ___.
- My favorite tool is ___.

For listening, allow students to look at a small image word bank before the second play. For the teacher session, accept short 3-4 sentence speaking with notes if needed.

## Extend This Week
Ask stronger learners to add one location sentence such as `The scissors are on the table` or one usefulness sentence such as `My sketchbook is useful because I draw ideas in it`. In the teacher session, they can answer a follow-up question about where an item is or why it matters in class.

## Asynchronous or App-Based Adaptation
The opener, vocabulary matching, visual reading, listening, phrase practice, and correction task can all be auto-checked or self-corrected in a future app. The My Studio Kit task should remain teacher-visible because it is the week’s meaningful writing output and includes revision support. The teacher-led speaking task should remain a non-recorded, teacher-observed checkpoint with sentence frames, a pronunciation focus list, and completion notes.
