weeks.lesson_plan_markdown:
# Week 5: Body, Figure, and Observation Drawing

## Overview
Week 5 moves from garment-only language into fashion-figure observation language. Students already know garment names and garment parts from Weeks 3 and 4. Now they begin to describe the drawn figure that wears the garment. The week stays visual, concrete, and A2-first. Students review one familiar figure image, learn body-reference and figure-sketch vocabulary, label a front-view figure, listen to pose descriptions, read short sketch captions, practice reliable phrase frames, build a scaffolded Fashion Figure Description Card, review one correction target, and describe one sketch in a teacher-supported speaking session.

The main written artifact is not a paragraph. Students complete a short structured Fashion Figure Description Card with 5 to 6 required sentence-frame lines and 1 optional challenge line. This keeps the task professional and useful without asking A2 learners for long free writing.

## Learning Objectives
- Recognize and name basic body-reference points in English.
- Match body-reference and figure-sketch visuals to English vocabulary with Portuguese support when needed.
- Label one fashion figure with clear point-key support.
- Understand short spoken descriptions of pose, view, and garment details.
- Read short sketch captions and match them to visible figures.
- Use sentence frames such as `The figure is ...`, `The figure is wearing ...`, `This is a front view`, `The silhouette is ...`, and `The hem is below the knee`.
- Complete a short Fashion Figure Description Card using 5 to 6 required lines and 1 optional challenge line.
- Revise one sentence focused on missing `is`, `is wearing`, adjective order, or location language.
- Describe one fashion figure or sketch in 4 to 6 short spoken sentences during the teacher session.

## Professional Fashion-Design Context
Week 5 connects English to observation drawing and fashion figure work. Fashion Design students often need to talk about the figure, the pose, the silhouette, and the visible garment on the figure before they move into fuller critique or portfolio writing. This language supports croquis reading, sketch description, early silhouette discussion, and future work in drawing, styling, and design presentation.

The body-reference language in this week should stay respectful and design-focused. Students are not evaluating a real person’s body. They are naming points on a drawn figure and describing pose, proportion, garment fit, silhouette, and visible design features.

## Language Objectives
- Name body-reference points such as `head`, `neck`, `shoulder`, `arm`, `waist`, `hip`, `leg`, `knee`, and `foot`.
- Use figure and sketch vocabulary such as `figure`, `sketch`, `croquis`, `outline`, `pose`, `proportion`, and `silhouette`.
- Use view and direction language such as `front view`, `side view`, `back view`, `standing`, `walking`, and `sitting`.
- Use guided description frames such as `The figure is standing`, `The figure is wearing a dress`, `The silhouette is long and simple`, and `The outline is clear`.
- Use location phrases such as `above the knee` and `below the knee` with obvious visual support.
- Improve adjective order in simple design phrases such as `simple outline`, `long silhouette`, and `relaxed pose`.

## Materials Needed
- One fashion figure opener board for review and preview.
- One body-reference-points diagram with clear labeled points.
- One figure-sketch vocabulary board or croquis concept board.
- One single front-view figure image with explicit point keys for labeling.
- One reusable four-figure gallery for listening, reading, writing, and speaking.
- One short audio clip or teacher read-aloud fallback for the listening task.
- Visible sentence frames for the Week 5 language focus.
- Student writing space for the Fashion Figure Description Card.

## Suggested Sequence
1. `m01w05-a01` Welcome Back: students review garments and notice the move from garment language to figure language.
2. `m01w05-a02` Body and Figure Vocabulary: students complete the two main image-match sets, then use a short Portuguese bridge and one fill-blank item as support.
3. `m01w05-a03` Label the Fashion Figure: students match body-reference words to explicit point keys on one front-view figure.
4. `m01w05-a04` Listen: students hear four short pose-and-view descriptions and choose the correct image or detail answer.
5. `m01w05-a05` Read: students read four sketch captions and match them to the four-figure gallery.
6. `m01w05-a06` Phrase Practice: students complete controlled frames with pose, view, garment, silhouette, outline, and hem-location language.
7. `m01w05-a07` Fashion Figure Description Card: students choose one figure and complete a structured writing card with required lines.
8. `m01w05-a08` Review and Improve: students correct one common Week 5 sentence problem.
9. `m01w05-a09` Teacher Session: students practice pronunciation, name body-reference points, and describe one sketch with support.

## Timing Estimate
- `m01w05-a01` 6 minutes
- `m01w05-a02` 14 minutes
- `m01w05-a03` 12 minutes
- `m01w05-a04` 12 minutes
- `m01w05-a05` 12 minutes
- `m01w05-a06` 10 minutes
- `m01w05-a07` 18 minutes
- `m01w05-a08` 7 minutes
- `m01w05-a09` 50 minutes

Total planned time: 141 minutes.

The asynchronous or app-style portion is 91 minutes. The teacher-led speaking session is 50 minutes.

## Differentiation Options
- Keep the body-reference diagram and four-figure gallery visible during vocabulary, listening, reading, and writing.
- Reduce the required labeling task to 6 points before adding the optional extra points.
- Provide a reduced word bank for the Fashion Figure Description Card if students need stronger support.
- Let students choose between a simpler front-view figure and a more complex walking figure based on confidence.
- During speaking, allow learners to point to the image while they speak.

## Extension Options
- Ask stronger learners to use the optional challenge line with `outline`, `body line`, or one extra reason sentence.
- Invite stronger learners to compare two figures with one short contrast sentence.
- In the teacher session, ask one follow-up question about silhouette, pose, or garment fit.

## Notes for Future App Implementation
Week 5 should remain image-first and highly aligned across tasks in a future app. The app-facing flow should preserve:

- one opener board for quick review and preview
- two main image-word matching sets as the primary saved vocabulary output
- one figure-labeling task with explicit point keys such as `A-H`
- one listening task whose audio script matches the image gallery and answer key exactly
- one reading task that reuses the same four-figure gallery with explicit image keys such as `image A`, `image B`, `image C`, and `image D`
- one phrase-practice task centered on fill-blank sentence frames as the main saved output
- one teacher-reviewed structured writing card with separate sentence-frame fields instead of a paragraph box
- one teacher-observed speaking checkpoint that displays prompts and tracks completion without recording audio

The Week 5 four-figure gallery should stay reusable in later weeks about sketch description, color, line, silhouette, and design feedback.
weeks.teacher_notes_markdown:
# Teacher Notes: Week 5 - Body, Figure, and Observation Drawing

## Common Learner Difficulties
Students may confuse body-reference points that are close together, especially `neck` and `shoulder`, or `waist` and `hip`. They may also mix Week 4 garment-part language with Week 5 figure language, for example using `waistband` when the target word is `waist`. Another common problem is grammar: `The figure standing`, `The figure is using a dress`, `This is front view`, or `The silhouette is simple long`.

## Classroom Management Suggestions
Keep the body-reference diagram and the four-figure gallery visible throughout the week. Students should not have to imagine the figure without image support at this stage. Move from recognition to production in a steady sequence: review, match, label, listen, read, complete frames, then write and speak. During the Fashion Figure Description Card, encourage students to complete one line at a time rather than trying to write a paragraph.

## Professional Context Notes
Keep the language connected to observation drawing, croquis work, and design description. Students are learning how to identify body-reference points on a drawn figure, name the pose and the view, and describe how the garment looks on the figure. The week should sound like beginner Fashion Design observation language, not like general appearance commentary.

## Cultural or Industry Notes
Some learners may already know the word `croquis` from Fashion Design classes, while others may prefer `sketch`. Present both clearly and keep `croquis` tied to fashion-drawing context. Also remind students that `silhouette` and `proportion` are common design words, but Week 5 uses them lightly and observationally rather than technically.

## Simplify This Week
Reduce the Fashion Figure Description Card to exactly five required lines:
- This is a fashion figure / sketch / croquis.
- The figure is standing / walking / sitting.
- This is a front view / side view / back view.
- The figure is wearing ___.
- The silhouette is ___.

Accept one visible detail sentence only if needed: `The garment has ___`. For Activity 3, keep only six required point labels. In the speaking task, accept 3 to 4 short spoken sentences with strong teacher prompting if needed.

## Extend This Week
Ask stronger learners to use the optional challenge line with `outline`, `body line`, or a short preference reason. During the teacher session, invite a follow-up sentence about why the pose is clear, why the silhouette is simple, or how the garment shape works on the figure.

## Asynchronous or App-Based Adaptation
The opener, vocabulary matching, labeling task, listening task, reading task, phrase-practice task, and correction task can all be app-checked with immediate feedback. The Fashion Figure Description Card should remain teacher-visible because it is the main written artifact and benefits from a small revision cycle. The speaking checkpoint should remain teacher-observed and non-recorded, with the app serving only to display the image gallery, sentence frames, and completion notes.

weeks.lesson_plan_markdown:
# Week 6: Color, Shape, and Line

## Overview
Week 6 introduces the English students need to describe what a look looks like visually. After Weeks 3 to 5, students can already name garments, garment parts, and figure features. This week adds color, palette, shape, line, silhouette, and simple visual-impression language so students can move from naming an item to describing the whole look. The week stays visual, concrete, and A2-first.

The main written artifact is not a paragraph. Students complete a scaffolded Color + Shape Look Description with 6 required sentence-frame lines and 1 optional challenge sentence. This keeps the task aligned with early Module 1 writing guardrails while still preparing students for later portfolio-style captions and design-description work.

## Learning Objectives
- Recognize and name basic colors and color-family words in English.
- Identify simple palette types such as warm, cool, neutral, bright, soft, and monochrome.
- Match shape, line, and silhouette vocabulary to clear visual examples.
- Read short visual look descriptions and connect them to the correct keyed images.
- Listen to short spoken look descriptions and identify the correct image or detail.
- Use simple frames such as `The color is ...`, `The palette is ...`, `The silhouette is ...`, `The lines are ...`, and `This look is ...`.
- Practice adjective order in phrases such as `a long black dress` and `a soft pink blouse`.
- Complete a scaffolded look-description card with 6 required lines and 1 optional challenge line.
- Describe one look orally in 4 to 6 short sentences during the teacher session.

## Professional Fashion-Design Context
Week 6 connects English to beginner drawing classes, creativity labs, look analysis, and early design description. Fashion Design students need this language when they talk about sketches, silhouettes, color palettes, and visual impressions before they explain deeper concept or technical details.

The week also prepares students for later modules on textiles, moodboards, styling, collections, portfolio captions, and design feedback. The focus should stay on respectful visual observation and design language, not on personal judgment about bodies or appearance.

## Language Objectives
- Name basic colors such as `black`, `white`, `red`, `blue`, `green`, `yellow`, `pink`, `purple`, `orange`, `brown`, and `gray`.
- Use palette words such as `warm`, `cool`, `neutral`, `bright`, `soft`, `monochrome`, and `contrast`.
- Use line and shape language such as `straight line`, `curved line`, `vertical line`, `horizontal line`, `diagonal line`, `round`, `square`, and `triangular`.
- Use silhouette and garment-shape words such as `loose`, `fitted`, `straight`, `flared`, `oversized`, and `cropped`.
- Use description frames such as `The palette is warm`, `The silhouette is long and straight`, `The lines are curved`, and `I like the look because it is simple`.
- Improve adjective order in simple garment phrases such as `a long black dress` and `wide blue pants`.

## Materials Needed
- One Week 6 opener board with 3 to 4 clearly different looks.
- One color swatch and palette board with visible keys.
- One shape, line, and silhouette board with visible keys.
- One three-look reading gallery labeled `image A`, `image B`, and `image C`.
- One reusable four-look gallery labeled `image A`, `image B`, `image C`, and `image D`.
- One short listening audio clip or teacher read-aloud fallback for the listening task.
- Visible sentence frames for the Week 6 language focus.
- Student writing space for the Color + Shape Look Description.

## Suggested Sequence
1. `m01w06-a01` Welcome Back: students look at a multi-look board and choose what they notice first.
2. `m01w06-a02` Color Vocabulary and Palettes: students complete the main color and palette matching set, then use a short Portuguese bridge and one support item.
3. `m01w06-a03` Shape, Line, and Silhouette: students complete the main shape-line-silhouette matching set and use one support item after the core matching.
4. `m01w06-a04` Read: students match three short visual descriptions to `image A`, `image B`, or `image C` and answer detail questions.
5. `m01w06-a05` Listen: students hear four short look descriptions and choose the matching image or key detail.
6. `m01w06-a06` Phrase Practice: students complete adjective-order and look-description frames with fill-blank support.
7. `m01w06-a07` Color + Shape Look Description: students choose one look and complete a teacher-reviewed structured writing card.
8. `m01w06-a08` Review and Improve: students correct one common Week 6 sentence problem.
9. `m01w06-a09` Teacher Session: students practice pronunciation and describe one look in short supported sentences.

## Timing Estimate
- `m01w06-a01` 6 minutes
- `m01w06-a02` 14 minutes
- `m01w06-a03` 14 minutes
- `m01w06-a04` 12 minutes
- `m01w06-a05` 12 minutes
- `m01w06-a06` 10 minutes
- `m01w06-a07` 18 minutes
- `m01w06-a08` 7 minutes
- `m01w06-a09` 50 minutes

Total planned time: 143 minutes.

The asynchronous or app-style portion is 93 minutes. The teacher-led speaking session is 50 minutes.

## Differentiation Options
- Keep the color board, shape board, and image galleries visible during vocabulary, reading, listening, writing, and speaking.
- Reduce the number of required palette terms for learners who need more support.
- Allow students to choose from two simpler looks before moving to a more complex look for the writing task.
- Provide a reduced word bank for the writing card if students need more support with silhouette or palette language.
- Let students point to the image while speaking in the teacher session.

## Extension Options
- Ask stronger learners to add the optional challenge sentence comparing two visual elements in the same look.
- Invite stronger learners to add one reason sentence about why the palette or silhouette works.
- In the teacher session, ask one follow-up question about contrast, line direction, or visual impression.

## Notes for Future App Implementation
Week 6 should remain strongly image-first and tightly aligned across tasks in a future app. The app-facing flow should preserve:

- one opener board for quick preview and review
- one main color-and-palette matching set as the primary saved vocabulary output
- one main shape-line-silhouette matching set as the primary saved visual-vocabulary output
- one reading gallery with explicit visible keys `image A`, `image B`, and `image C`
- one listening task whose audio script matches the four-look gallery and answer key exactly
- one fill-blank phrase-practice task where the primary saved output stays phrase completion
- one teacher-reviewed structured writing card with separate sentence-frame fields instead of a paragraph box
- one teacher-observed speaking checkpoint that shows the gallery and frames but does not record audio

The Week 6 four-look gallery should stay reusable for listening, writing, speaking, and later visual-description work in future modules.
weeks.teacher_notes_markdown:
# Teacher Notes: Week 6 - Color, Shape, and Line

## Common Learner Difficulties
Students may confuse color words that are close in meaning or overuse only basic colors without adding palette or visual-impression language. They may also mix `shape`, `line`, and `silhouette` as if they mean the same thing. Another common difficulty is adjective order, especially in phrases like `a black long dress`, and agreement problems such as `The pants is blue` or `The color palette are warm`.

## Classroom Management Suggestions
Keep the Week 6 boards and galleries visible throughout the week. Students should be able to point to color, line, and silhouette examples while they answer. Move steadily from recognition to production: opener, color matching, shape-line matching, reading, listening, phrase practice, structured writing, correction, then speaking. During the writing task, encourage students to complete one sentence frame at a time instead of trying to produce a paragraph.

## Professional Context Notes
Keep the week connected to fashion drawing, beginner visual analysis, and look description. Students are not doing abstract art criticism. They are learning how to say what they see in a look: color palette, garment shapes, visible lines, silhouette, and overall impression. This language is useful for later sketch explanation, moodboards, styling comments, and short portfolio captions.

## Cultural or Industry Notes
Many learners may already know fashion words such as `silhouette`, `oversized`, or `cropped` from social media or design classes, but they may not know how to place them in a full English sentence. Keep the focus on accurate simple usage, not on sounding advanced. Also remind students that visual-impression words such as `modern`, `classic`, `casual`, and `playful` are design-description words, not personal judgments.

## Simplify This Week
Keep the writing card at exactly six required lines:
- This is a look / sketch / fashion figure.
- The color palette is ___.
- The figure is wearing ___.
- The silhouette is ___.
- The lines are ___.
- The look is ___.

Accept one optional challenge sentence only if the student is ready: `I like the ___ because ___.`. In the speaking task, accept 3 to 4 short spoken sentences with strong teacher prompting if needed.

## Extend This Week
Ask stronger learners to use the optional challenge sentence comparing two elements, for example `The top is fitted, but the pants are loose.` During the teacher session, invite one follow-up sentence explaining why the student likes the palette, silhouette, or contrast.

## Asynchronous or App-Based Adaptation
The opener, color matching, shape-line-silhouette matching, reading task, listening task, phrase-practice task, and correction task can all be app-checked with immediate feedback. The Color + Shape Look Description should remain teacher-visible because it is the main written artifact, uses 6 required lines plus 1 optional challenge sentence, and benefits from a small revision cycle. The speaking checkpoint should remain teacher-observed and non-recorded, with the app serving only to display the gallery, sentence frames, and completion notes.

expected_output.description_en: A short teacher-observed spoken description of one fabric using Week 7 sentence frames.
expected_output.description_pt: Uma descrição oral curta, observada pelo professor, de um tecido usando as estruturas da Semana 7.

completion_criteria_en: The student names one chosen fabric clearly.
The student uses feel, look, and use language in short sentences.
The student adds at least one clear reason or function detail with support if needed.
completion_criteria_pt: O aluno nomeia com clareza um tecido escolhido.
O aluno usa linguagem de toque, aparência e uso em frases curtas.
O aluno acrescenta pelo menos uma justificativa clara ou um detalhe de função com apoio, se necessário.
checklist_en: I practiced the Week 7 words.
I used my description card.
I described one fabric in short sentences.
checklist_pt: Eu pratiquei as palavras da Semana 7.
Eu usei o meu cartão de descrição.
Eu descrevi um tecido em frases curtas.
assessment.model_response_en: This is a silk fabric swatch. It feels smooth. It looks shiny. It is lightweight. It is good for elegant blouses. I like this fabric because it looks beautiful.
assessment.model_response_pt: Esta é uma amostra de seda. Ela parece lisa ao toque. Ela parece brilhante. Ela é leve. É boa para blusas elegantes. Eu gosto deste tecido porque ele parece bonito.
common_errors: Saying fabric names only and skipping the full sentence frames.
Using feels for visual qualities or looks for touch.
Speaking too quietly to be understood.
feedback_prompts_en: Can you add one feel sentence?
Can you say that again with looks or feels in the best place?
Can you add one use sentence?
feedback_prompts_pt: Você pode acrescentar uma frase sobre o toque?
Você pode dizer novamente com looks ou feels no melhor lugar?
Você pode acrescentar uma frase sobre o uso?

support: Allow students to read directly from the writing card in the first round.
challenge: Ask stronger learners one follow-up question about weather, comfort, or garment type.

extension_options: Add one extra spoken sentence comparing two swatches from the gallery.
activities.notes_for_app_design: Keep this as a teacher-observed speaking checkpoint with the shared swatch gallery and the saved Week 7 writing card visible on screen. Do not record or upload student audio. The app role is to display prompts, link to the writing artifact, and store teacher completion notes only.

vocabulary_groups.title: Fabric, textile, and swatch words
vocabulary_groups.description: Core naming words for fabric study, swatches, and beginner textile observation.

items.definition_en: Cloth or material used to make clothes.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: Cloth used for garments.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Tecido usado para roupas.
items.example_sentence_en: This fabric is soft.
items.example_sentence_pt: Este tecido é macio.
items.professional_context_en: Fabric is the main Week 7 word for textile and garment-material description.
items.professional_context_pt: Fabric é a principal palavra da Semana 7 para descrever têxteis e materiais de roupas.
items.translation_notes_pt: Use fabric como palavra principal para tecido.

items.definition_en: A broader technical word for fabric or cloth materials.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A general word for cloth material.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Uma palavra mais geral para material de tecido.
items.example_sentence_en: This textile is lightweight.
items.example_sentence_pt: Este têxtil é leve.
items.professional_context_en: Textile is useful as a support-tier word for later fabric, sustainability, and design-study work.
items.professional_context_pt: Textile é útil como palavra de apoio para trabalhos futuros sobre tecidos, sustentabilidade e estudos de design.
items.translation_notes_pt: Explique textile como uma palavra mais técnica e geral do que fabric.

items.definition_en: The substance used to make a garment or object.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: What something is made from.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Aquilo de que algo é feito.
items.example_sentence_en: The material is smooth.
items.example_sentence_pt: O material é liso.
items.professional_context_en: Material is a useful general design word when students talk about garment choice or function.
items.professional_context_pt: Material é uma palavra geral útil de design quando os alunos falam sobre escolha de roupa ou função.
items.translation_notes_pt: Material é parecido com o português, mas continue mantendo fabric como a palavra central para tecido.

items.definition_en: A small sample piece of fabric.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A small piece of fabric for study or choice.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um pequeno pedaço de tecido para estudo ou escolha.
items.example_sentence_en: This is a fabric swatch.
items.example_sentence_pt: Esta é uma amostra de tecido.
items.professional_context_en: Fabric swatch is a key Week 7 phrase for material observation and the main writing artifact.
items.professional_context_pt: Fabric swatch é uma expressão central da Semana 7 para observação de materiais e para a principal produção escrita.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais útil é amostra de tecido.

items.definition_en: A small example of a material.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A small example piece.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Uma pequena peça de exemplo.
items.example_sentence_en: These are fabric samples.
items.example_sentence_pt: Estas são amostras de tecido.
items.professional_context_en: Sample supports later work with swatches, moodboards, and material selection.
items.professional_context_pt: Sample ajuda em trabalhos futuros com amostras, moodboards e seleção de materiais.
items.translation_notes_pt: Explique como amostra; é contável em inglês.

vocabulary_groups.title: Common fabrics and materials
vocabulary_groups.description: Common material words students need for beginner garment and swatch description.

items.definition_en: A common soft natural fabric used for many clothes.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A soft common fabric.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um tecido comum e macio.
items.example_sentence_en: The shirt is made of cotton.
items.example_sentence_pt: A camisa é feita de algodão.
items.professional_context_en: Cotton is a core material example for comfort, summer clothing, and breathable fabrics.
items.professional_context_pt: Cotton é um exemplo central de material para conforto, roupas de verão e tecidos respiráveis.
items.translation_notes_pt: Use cotton sem artigo em frases simples como This is cotton.

items.definition_en: A strong fabric often used for jeans and jackets.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A strong blue fabric for jeans.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um tecido forte, muito usado em jeans.
items.example_sentence_en: The jacket is made of denim.
items.example_sentence_pt: A jaqueta é feita de denim.

items.professional_context_pt: Denim é um material visualmente fácil para trabalhar estrutura, peso e uso da roupa.
items.translation_notes_pt: Os alunos podem associar a jeans ou brim; mantenha denim como alvo em inglês.

items.definition_en: A natural fabric often used for light and cool clothing.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A light fabric often used in warm weather.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um tecido leve, muito usado em clima quente.
items.example_sentence_en: Linen is good for hot weather.
items.example_sentence_pt: Linho é bom para clima quente.
items.professional_context_en: Linen helps students connect fabric choice to weather and comfort.
items.professional_context_pt: Linen ajuda os alunos a relacionar a escolha do tecido com clima e conforto.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é linho.

items.definition_en: A smooth fabric that often looks shiny and elegant.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A smooth elegant fabric.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um tecido liso e elegante.
items.example_sentence_en: The blouse is made of silk.
items.example_sentence_pt: A blusa é feita de seda.
items.professional_context_en: Silk is useful for smooth, shiny, lightweight, and elegant fabric description.
items.professional_context_pt: Silk é útil para descrever tecidos lisos, brilhantes, leves e elegantes.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é seda.

items.definition_en: A warm fabric often used for colder weather.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A warm fabric for cold weather.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um tecido quente para clima frio.
items.example_sentence_en: Wool is good for cold weather.
items.example_sentence_pt: Lã é boa para clima frio.
items.professional_context_en: Wool helps students connect fabric to warmth, thickness, and winter garments.
items.professional_context_pt: Wool ajuda os alunos a ligar o tecido a calor, espessura e roupas de inverno.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é lã.

items.definition_en: A common synthetic fabric used in many garments.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A common artificial fabric.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um tecido sintético comum.
items.example_sentence_en: The skirt is made of polyester.
items.example_sentence_pt: A saia é feita de poliéster.
items.professional_context_en: Polyester adds useful contrast to natural materials in beginner textile vocabulary.
items.professional_context_pt: Polyester acrescenta um contraste útil com materiais naturais no vocabulário têxtil inicial.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é poliéster.

items.definition_en: Fabric made with loops that is often stretchy.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A fabric that is often soft and stretchy.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um tecido que costuma ser macio e elástico.
items.example_sentence_en: Knit fabric is often stretchy.
items.example_sentence_pt: Tecido de malha costuma ser elástico.
items.professional_context_en: Knit fabric is a useful support-tier term for fabric behavior and sewing vocabulary.
items.professional_context_pt: Knit fabric é um termo útil de apoio para comportamento do tecido e vocabulário de costura.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais útil é tecido de malha ou malha.

items.definition_en: Fabric made with crossing threads that is often more stable.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A fabric with crossing threads, often less stretchy.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um tecido com fios cruzados, geralmente menos elástico.
items.example_sentence_en: Woven fabric is often more stable.
items.example_sentence_pt: Tecido plano costuma ser mais estável.
items.professional_context_en: Woven fabric supports early textile observation and later sewing vocabulary.
items.professional_context_pt: Woven fabric apoia a observação têxtil inicial e o vocabulário futuro de costura.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais útil é tecido plano.

items.definition_en: A decorative fabric with open areas or holes.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A decorative fabric with visible open parts.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um tecido decorativo com partes abertas visíveis.
items.example_sentence_en: The sleeve is made of lace.
items.example_sentence_pt: A manga é feita de renda.
items.professional_context_en: Lace is useful for texture, transparency, and decorative-use language.
items.professional_context_pt: Lace é útil para linguagem de textura, transparência e uso decorativo.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é renda.

items.definition_en: A strong material often used for jackets, shoes, or bags.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A strong material for jackets, shoes, or bags.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um material forte para jaquetas, sapatos ou bolsas.
items.example_sentence_en: The bag is made of leather.
items.example_sentence_pt: A bolsa é feita de couro.
items.professional_context_en: Leather supports material-choice discussion for structure, strength, and garment or accessory use.
items.professional_context_pt: Leather apoia a discussão sobre escolha de material para estrutura, resistência e uso em roupa ou acessório.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é couro.

vocabulary_groups.title: Texture and surface qualities
vocabulary_groups.description: Core feel and surface words for describing how a fabric feels and how it looks.

items.definition_en: Pleasant and gentle to touch.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: Nice and gentle to touch.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Agradável e suave ao toque.
items.example_sentence_en: The fabric feels soft.
items.example_sentence_pt: O tecido é macio ao toque.
items.professional_context_en: Soft is one of the most useful beginner touch words for fabric description.
items.professional_context_pt: Soft é uma das palavras iniciais mais úteis para falar do toque do tecido.

items.definition_en: Not smooth; with a harder surface feel.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: Not smooth to touch.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Não liso ao toque.

items.definition_en: Even and not rough to touch.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: Nice and not rough.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Liso e não áspero.
items.example_sentence_en: The fabric feels smooth.
items.example_sentence_pt: O tecido é liso ao toque.
items.professional_context_en: Smooth supports both touch description and silk-like fabric observation.

items.definition_en: Reflecting light and looking bright on the surface.

items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Com aparência brilhante porque reflete luz.
items.example_sentence_en: The silk looks shiny.
items.example_sentence_pt: A seda parece brilhante.
items.professional_context_en: Shiny is a key visual word for silk-like surfaces and elegant fabric description.
items.professional_context_pt: Shiny é uma palavra visual central para superfícies parecidas com seda e descrições elegantes de tecido.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é brilhante.

items.definition_en: Not shiny; without a bright reflective surface.

items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Sem brilho na superfície.
items.example_sentence_en: The fabric looks matte.
items.example_sentence_pt: O tecido parece fosco.

items.professional_context_pt: Matte ajuda os alunos a contrastar a aparência da superfície com clareza.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é fosco ou fosca.

items.definition_en: Having a surface with visible or touchable variation.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: Not flat or plain on the surface.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Sem superfície plana; com textura visível.
items.example_sentence_en: The lace is textured.
items.example_sentence_pt: A renda é texturizada.
items.professional_context_en: Textured is a useful support word for closer textile observation.
items.professional_context_pt: Textured é uma palavra útil de apoio para observação têxtil mais detalhada.
items.translation_notes_pt: Pode ser explicado como texturizado ou com textura.

items.definition_en: Simple and without decoration or strong surface detail.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: Simple and not decorative.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Simples e sem decoração.
items.example_sentence_en: The fabric looks plain.
items.example_sentence_pt: O tecido parece simples.
items.professional_context_en: Plain helps students contrast decorative versus simple surface impression.
items.professional_context_pt: Plain ajuda os alunos a contrastar uma aparência de superfície decorativa com uma aparência simples.
items.translation_notes_pt: Pode ser simples ou liso, dependendo do contexto.

vocabulary_groups.title: Weight, movement, structure, and visibility

items.definition_en: Not heavy.

items.definition_en: Having a lot of weight.

items.definition_en: Having more depth or body.

items.definition_en: Not thick.

items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Fino e não grosso.
items.example_sentence_en: The fabric is thin.

items.professional_context_en: Thin helps students describe lighter fabric body and compare materials.
items.professional_context_pt: Thin ajuda os alunos a descrever um corpo de tecido mais leve e a comparar materiais.

items.definition_en: Able to stretch easily.

items.professional_context_pt: Stretchy é uma palavra central de comportamento do tecido na Semana 7 para conforto e caimento.

items.definition_en: Not easy to bend or move.

items.professional_context_pt: Stiff ajuda os alunos a descrever estrutura e pouca movimentação do material.

items.definition_en: Easy to bend or move.

items.definition_en: Moving softly and easily.

items.definition_en: Easy to see through.

items.definition_en: Very light and partly transparent.

items.example_sentence_en: The fabric is opaque.

vocabulary_groups.title: Use, comfort, and material-description phrases
vocabulary_groups.description: Simple reusable phrases for saying what a fabric feels like, what it is made of, and what it suits.

items.definition_en: Feeling good and easy to wear.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: Nice and easy to wear.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Bom e fácil de usar.

weeks.lesson_plan_markdown:
# Week 7: Fabric and Texture Basics

## Overview
Week 7 introduces the English students need to describe what a fabric is like. After Week 6, students can already describe color, shape, line, and silhouette. This week shifts from visual look description to textile observation: what the fabric is, how it feels, how it looks, how it moves, and what it is good for.

The main written artifact stays A2-first. Students do not write a paragraph and do not work toward a base word count. Instead, they complete a scaffolded Fabric Swatch Description Card with 6 required sentence-frame lines and 1 optional challenge sentence. This keeps the task concrete, reviewable, and aligned with early Module 1 writing guardrails.

## Learning Objectives
- Recognize and name common fabric and material words in English.
- Identify basic texture and surface qualities such as `soft`, `rough`, `smooth`, `shiny`, and `matte`.
- Identify simple weight, movement, structure, and visibility words such as `lightweight`, `heavy`, `stretchy`, `stiff`, `flowy`, `structured`, `transparent`, and `opaque`.
- Read short fabric-swatch descriptions and connect them to the correct keyed images.
- Listen to short spoken fabric descriptions and identify the correct swatch or key detail.
- Use simple frames such as `It is made of ...`, `It feels ...`, `It looks ...`, `It is good for ...`, and `It can be used for ...`.
- Complete a scaffolded fabric-description card with 6 required lines and 1 optional challenge line.
- Describe one fabric orally in 4 to 6 short sentences during the teacher session.

## Professional Fashion-Design Context
Week 7 connects English to introductory sewing, early textiles observation, garment planning, and design reasoning. Fashion Design students need this language when they discuss swatches, choose materials for a garment, compare comfort and movement, and explain why one fabric suits a dress, jacket, shirt, or detail better than another.

The week also prepares students for later work on textiles, sustainability, garment function, styling, portfolio captions, and collection concepts. The focus should stay concrete and observable: what the fabric is made of, how it feels, how it looks, and what it can be used for.

## Language Objectives
- Name common material words such as `fabric`, `material`, `fabric swatch`, `cotton`, `denim`, `linen`, `silk`, `wool`, `polyester`, `lace`, and `leather`.
- Recognize support words such as `textile`, `sample`, `knit fabric`, `woven fabric`, `sheer`, and `breathable`.
- Use feel and surface words such as `soft`, `rough`, `smooth`, `shiny`, `matte`, `textured`, and `plain`.
- Use behavior and visibility words such as `lightweight`, `heavy`, `stretchy`, `stiff`, `flowy`, `structured`, `transparent`, and `opaque`.
- Use description frames such as `This is denim`, `It feels soft`, `It looks shiny`, `It is made of cotton`, and `It is good for summer dresses`.
- Use the optional preference frame `I like this fabric because ...` when ready.

## Materials Needed
- One Week 7 opener board with 3 to 4 garments or swatches that clearly suggest different materials.
- One common-materials swatch board with visible keys.
- One texture-and-qualities board with visible keys.
- One three-swatch reading gallery labeled `image A`, `image B`, and `image C`.
- One reusable four-swatch gallery labeled `image A`, `image B`, `image C`, and `image D`.
- One short listening audio clip or teacher read-aloud fallback for the listening task.
- Visible sentence frames for the Week 7 language focus.
- Student writing space for the Fabric Swatch Description Card.
- Optional classroom support: real swatches or fabric samples for the teacher session.

## Suggested Sequence
1. `m01w07-a01` Welcome Back: students bridge from Week 6 visual language into Week 7 material language with a short opener.
2. `m01w07-a02` Fabric Vocabulary: students complete the main common-materials matching set, then use a short Portuguese bridge or support item.
3. `m01w07-a03` Texture and Material Qualities: students complete the main qualities matching set and use one support item after the core matching.
4. `m01w07-a04` Read: students match three short swatch descriptions to `image A`, `image B`, or `image C` and answer detail questions.
5. `m01w07-a05` Listen: students hear four short fabric descriptions and choose the matching image or key detail.
6. `m01w07-a06` Phrase Practice: students complete fill-blank frames using `made of`, `feels`, `looks`, and `good for`.
7. `m01w07-a07` Fabric Swatch Description Card: students choose one swatch and complete a teacher-reviewed structured writing card.
8. `m01w07-a08` Review and Improve: students correct one common Week 7 sentence problem.
9. `m01w07-a09` Teacher Session: students practice pronunciation and describe one fabric in short supported sentences.

## Timing Estimate
- `m01w07-a01` 6 minutes
- `m01w07-a02` 14 minutes
- `m01w07-a03` 14 minutes
- `m01w07-a04` 12 minutes
- `m01w07-a05` 12 minutes
- `m01w07-a06` 10 minutes
- `m01w07-a07` 18 minutes
- `m01w07-a08` 7 minutes
- `m01w07-a09` 50 minutes

Total planned time: 143 minutes.

The asynchronous or app-style portion is 93 minutes. The teacher-led speaking session is 50 minutes.

## Differentiation Options
- Keep the swatch boards and galleries visible during vocabulary, reading, listening, writing, and speaking.
- Reduce the number of active production words for learners who need more support and keep `textile`, `breathable`, and `flexible` as recognition words only.
- Let students choose from two easier swatches before moving to a more complex swatch for the writing task.
- Provide a reduced word bank for the writing card if students need more support with visibility or movement words.
- Let students point to the swatch while speaking in the teacher session.

## Extension Options
- Ask stronger learners to add the optional challenge sentence with a clearer design reason.
- Invite stronger learners to add one short comparison such as `This fabric is lighter than denim.` during speaking only if the teacher wants light extension.
- In the teacher session, ask one follow-up question about weather, comfort, or garment type.

## Notes for Future App Implementation
Week 7 should stay strongly image-first and tightly aligned across tasks in a future app. The app-facing flow should preserve:

- one opener board for fast bridge and preview work
- one main common-materials matching set as the primary saved vocabulary output
- one main texture-and-qualities matching set as the primary saved visual-vocabulary output
- one reading gallery with explicit visible keys `image A`, `image B`, and `image C`
- one listening task whose audio script matches the four-swatch gallery and answer key exactly
- one fill-blank phrase-practice task where the primary saved output stays phrase completion
- one teacher-reviewed structured writing card with separate sentence-frame fields instead of a paragraph box
- one teacher-observed speaking checkpoint that shows the gallery and frames but does not record audio

The Week 7 four-swatch gallery should stay reusable for listening, writing, and speaking, and should use the same fabric set and visible image keys across those tasks.
weeks.teacher_notes_markdown:
# Teacher Notes: Week 7 - Fabric and Texture Basics

## Common Learner Difficulties
Students may confuse what the fabric feels like with what it looks like, especially with pairs such as `soft` versus `shiny` and `rough` versus `matte`. They may also forget `of` in `made of`, treat fabric nouns like countable items in simple sentences, or choose too many words at once without forming a full sentence. Another common difficulty is using support-tier words such as `breathable` or `textile` before they are comfortable with the core Week 7 set.

## Classroom Management Suggestions
Keep the Week 7 boards and galleries visible throughout the week. Students should be able to point to a swatch while they answer. Move steadily from recognition to production: opener, material matching, quality matching, reading, listening, phrase practice, structured writing, correction, then speaking. During the writing task, encourage students to complete one line at a time instead of trying to write a paragraph.

## Professional Context Notes
Keep the week connected to swatches, samples, simple fabric choice, and beginner sewing or garment-planning decisions. Students are not doing advanced textile science. They are learning how to say what a material is, how it feels, how it looks, and what garment or weather use it suits. This language is useful later for textiles, sustainability, product description, collection planning, and styling discussions.

## Cultural or Industry Notes
Many learners may already know a few fashion or retail words such as `denim`, `lace`, or `cropped`, but they may not know how to place them in clear English frames. Keep the focus on accurate, simple usage rather than on sounding advanced. Also remind students that some fabric words remain uncountable in simple use, as in `This is cotton` rather than `a cotton`.

## Simplify This Week
Keep the writing card at exactly six required lines:
- `This is ...` or `This is a ... fabric swatch.`
- `It is ...`
- `It feels ...`
- `It looks ...`
- `It is ...`
- `It is good for ...` or `It can be used for ...`

Accept one optional challenge sentence only if the student is ready: `I like this fabric because ...`. In the speaking task, accept 4 short spoken sentences with strong teacher prompting if needed.

## Extend This Week
Ask stronger learners to use the optional challenge sentence with a clear reason linked to garment type, comfort, or season. During the teacher session, invite one follow-up sentence comparing two fabrics or explaining why a fabric suits a silhouette.

## Asynchronous or App-Based Adaptation
The opener, materials matching, qualities matching, reading task, listening task, phrase-practice task, and correction task can all be app-checked with immediate feedback. The Fabric Swatch Description Card should remain teacher-visible because it is the main written artifact, uses 6 required lines plus 1 optional challenge sentence, and benefits from a small revision cycle. The speaking checkpoint should remain teacher-observed and non-recorded, with the app serving only to display the gallery, sentence frames, and completion notes.

assessment.model_response_en: First, measure the fabric. Then, mark the line. Next, cut the fabric. After that, fold the edge and pin it. Use scissors to cut the fabric. Finally, check the stitches. Optional challenge: This step is important because the line should stay straight.
assessment.model_response_pt: First, measure the fabric. Then, mark the line. Next, cut the fabric. After that, fold the edge and pin it. Use scissors to cut the fabric. Finally, check the stitches. Desafio opcional: This step is important because the line should stay straight.
common_errors: Writing a list of words instead of complete sentence-frame lines.
Forgetting to use a sequence word at the start of a line.
Leaving out to in the tool phrase Use ___ to ___.
Treating the optional challenge line like a required line.
Turning the task into a paragraph instead of separate line fields.
feedback_prompts_en: Please complete one line as a full sentence.
Please check the sequence order again.
Please add one clearer tool phrase.
Please revise one line and submit again.
feedback_prompts_pt: Por favor, complete uma linha como frase inteira.
Por favor, confira novamente a ordem da sequência.
Por favor, acrescente uma frase mais clara com ferramenta.
Por favor, revise uma linha e envie novamente.

support: Let students complete exactly six core lines with a visible word bank and one model line on screen.
challenge: Invite stronger learners to add the optional challenge line with a clear reason linked to quality, order, or tool choice.

extension_options: Turn one line from the card into a speaking note for the teacher session.
activities.notes_for_app_design: Render this as a teacher-reviewed structured writing card with the shared gallery visible and separate saved line fields, not a paragraph text box. Keep 6 lines required, 1 challenge line optional, and show the teacher the checklist, common errors, feedback prompts, and return-for-revision workflow.

activities.title: Review and Improve: Clear Process Sentences
activities.summary: Students improve short sewing-process sentences by correcting one clear error at a time and submitting two corrected sentences for app checking.

en.title: Review and Improve: Clear Process Sentences
en.summary: Read each short sentence, find the mistake, and write the corrected sentence.
en.instructions: Look at one correction card at a time. Read the short sewing sentence, find the mistake, and rewrite the sentence correctly. Write two corrected sentences.
success_criteria: I can notice one mistake in a short process sentence.
I can rewrite the sentence clearly in English.
I can keep my correction short and accurate.

pt.title: Reveja e melhore: frases claras de processo
pt.summary: Leia cada frase curta, encontre o erro e escreva a frase corrigida.
pt.instructions: Observe um cartao de correcao por vez. Leia a frase curta de costura, encontre o erro e reescreva a frase corretamente. Escreva duas frases corrigidas.
success_criteria: Eu consigo perceber um erro em uma frase curta de processo.
Eu consigo reescrever a frase com clareza em ingles.
Eu consigo manter minha correcao curta e correta.

activities.teacher_instructions: Keep the task focused on visible sentence correction only. Students should correct two short sentences and the app should check against accepted answers, not teacher judgment.

input.prompt_en: Correct the short sewing-process sentences.
input.prompt_pt: Corrija as frases curtas de processo de costura.

items.label_pt: Cartao de correcao 1
items.student_prompt_en: Rewrite the sentence with the correct sequence punctuation and object.
items.student_prompt_pt: Reescreva a frase com a pontuacao correta da sequencia e com o objeto correto.

items.label_pt: Cartao de correcao 2
items.student_prompt_en: Rewrite the sentence with the correct tool phrase.
items.student_prompt_pt: Reescreva a frase com a expressao correta de ferramenta.
accepted_answers: Use scissors to cut the fabric.
Use the scissors to cut the fabric.

steps.title: Read the first correction card
steps.student_action_en: Read the first short sentence and notice the sequence problem.
steps.student_action_pt: Leia a primeira frase curta e perceba o problema de sequencia e de completude.
steps.teacher_action: Remind students to compare the sentence with the frame shown on the card.

steps.title: Rewrite the corrected sentence
steps.student_action_en: Write the corrected sentence for the first card, then repeat the process for the second card.
steps.student_action_pt: Escreva a frase corrigida do primeiro cartao e depois repita o processo no segundo cartao.
steps.teacher_action: Encourage short accurate rewrites instead of longer explanations.

steps.title: Check and submit
steps.student_action_en: Read both corrected sentences again and submit them.
steps.student_action_pt: Leia novamente as duas frases corrigidas e envie as respostas.
steps.teacher_action: Point out that the task checks exact sentence correction, not extra details.

expected_output.description_en: Two corrected sewing-process sentences checked by the app.
expected_output.description_pt: Duas frases corrigidas de processo de costura verificadas pelo app.

completion_criteria_en: The student rewrites both sentences correctly.
The student uses the visible sentence frame or tool phrase correctly.
The student keeps each correction short and complete.
completion_criteria_pt: O aluno reescreve as duas frases corretamente.
O aluno usa corretamente a estrutura visivel da frase ou a expressao com ferramenta.
O aluno mantem cada correcao curta e completa.
checklist_en: I fixed the sequence frame in sentence 1.
I used Use ___ to ___ correctly in sentence 2.
I submitted two complete corrected sentences.
checklist_pt: Eu corrigi a estrutura de sequencia na frase 1.
Eu usei Use ___ to ___ corretamente na frase 2.
Eu enviei duas frases corrigidas completas.
assessment.model_response_en: Then, cut the fabric carefully. Use scissors to cut the fabric.
assessment.model_response_pt: Then, cut the fabric carefully. Use scissors to cut the fabric.
common_errors: Leaving out the object in the first correction.
Leaving out to in the tool phrase.
Adding extra ideas that are not needed for the correction.
feedback_prompts_en: Which sequence word should start this sentence?
Does your tool phrase include to after the tool?
feedback_prompts_pt: Qual objeto esta faltando nesta frase?
Sua frase com ferramenta inclui to depois da ferramenta?

support: Let students reread the visible sentence frame before they type the correction.
challenge: Ask stronger learners to explain orally why each corrected sentence is better.

extension_options: Turn one corrected sentence into a model line for the speaking task.
activities.notes_for_app_design: Render one correction card at a time. Save two corrected sentences as the main output and check them against explicit accepted answers only.

activities.title: Teacher Session: Explain the Steps
activities.summary: Students use the shared process board and their writing card to explain a short sewing sequence aloud in a teacher-observed speaking routine.

en.title: Teacher Session: Explain the Steps
en.summary: Look at the process board and explain the steps aloud in short English sentences.
en.instructions: Use the process board and your process card. Say 5 to 6 short steps aloud. Use sequence words and at least one tool phrase.
success_criteria: I can say the steps in order.
I can use short clear sewing words in English.
I can include at least one tool phrase.

pt.title: Sessao com o professor: explique as etapas
pt.summary: Observe o painel de processo e explique as etapas em voz alta com frases curtas em ingles.
pt.instructions: Use o painel de processo e o seu cartao de processo. Diga 5 a 6 etapas curtas em voz alta. Use palavras de sequencia e pelo menos uma frase com ferramenta.
success_criteria: Eu consigo dizer as etapas em ordem.
Eu consigo usar palavras curtas e claras de costura em ingles.
Eu consigo incluir pelo menos uma frase com ferramenta.

activities.teacher_instructions: This is a teacher-observed speaking task only. Do not require recording, upload, or automated scoring. Keep the output scaffolded and short by using the process board and the student's card as speaking supports.

input.prompt_en: Use the board and your process card to explain the simple sewing process aloud.
input.prompt_pt: Use o painel e o seu cartao de processo para explicar em voz alta o processo simples de costura.

items.label_pt: Tarefa de fala
items.prompt_en: Explain the steps from image A to image E in 5 to 6 short sentences.
items.prompt_pt: Explique as etapas da sequencia marcada de "image A" a "image E" em 5 a 6 frases curtas.

steps.title: Review the board and card
steps.student_action_en: Look at the process board and your process card before you speak.
steps.student_action_pt: Observe o painel de processo e o seu cartao de processo antes de falar.
steps.teacher_action: Give students a short preparation moment with the visible sequence frames.

steps.title: Explain the steps aloud
steps.student_action_en: Say 5 to 6 short process steps aloud in order and include one tool phrase.
steps.student_action_pt: Diga em voz alta 5 a 6 etapas curtas de processo em ordem e inclua uma frase com ferramenta.
steps.teacher_action: Observe for clarity, sequence words, tool phrase use, and key pronunciation targets.

steps.title: Close with brief feedback
steps.student_action_en: Listen to one short teacher comment about your speaking.
steps.student_action_pt: Escute um comentario curto do professor sobre a sua fala.
steps.teacher_action: Give one strength and one next-step note. Keep the feedback brief and supportive.

expected_output.description_en: One teacher-observed spoken explanation of a simple sewing process with 5 to 6 short steps.
expected_output.description_pt: Uma explicacao oral observada pelo professor sobre um processo simples de costura com 5 a 6 etapas curtas.

completion_criteria_en: The student explains the steps in a clear order.
The student uses sequence words and at least one tool phrase.
The student completes a short spoken explanation without recording or upload.
completion_criteria_pt: O aluno explica as etapas em uma ordem clara.
O aluno usa palavras de sequencia e pelo menos uma frase com ferramenta.
O aluno completa uma explicacao oral curta sem gravacao nem envio.
checklist_en: The student says 5 to 6 short steps.
The student uses at least one tool phrase.
The student uses understandable pronunciation for key sewing words.
The student stays on the visible process path.
checklist_pt: O aluno diz 5 a 6 etapas curtas.
O aluno usa pelo menos uma frase com ferramenta.
O aluno usa pronuncia compreensivel para palavras-chave de costura.
O aluno permanece no caminho de processo visivel.
assessment.model_response_en: First, measure the fabric. Then, mark the line. Next, cut the fabric. After that, fold the edge and pin it. Use scissors to cut the fabric. Finally, check the stitches.
assessment.model_response_pt: First, measure the fabric. Then, mark the line. Next, cut the fabric. After that, fold the edge and pin it. Use scissors to cut the fabric. Finally, check the stitches.
common_errors: Skipping sequence words.
Switching the order of the visible process steps.
Speaking in single words instead of short sentences.
Trying to record instead of speaking live to the teacher.
feedback_prompts_en: Please say the steps again with sequence words.
Please add one tool phrase to your explanation.
Please keep your sentences short and clear.
feedback_prompts_pt: Por favor, diga novamente as etapas com palavras de sequencia.
Por favor, acrescente uma frase com ferramenta a sua explicacao.
Por favor, mantenha suas frases curtas e claras.

support: Let students keep the process card visible while they speak.
challenge: Invite stronger learners to add one reason sentence after the final step.

extension_options: Pair students for one extra rehearsal before the next live explanation.
activities.notes_for_app_design: Show the speaking frame and image board as supports, but store only teacher observation/completion data. Do not add recording, upload, or automated speech scoring.

vocabulary_groups.title: Sewing actions
vocabulary_groups.description: Core action words students need for simple sewing-process instructions.

items.definition_en: To divide fabric with scissors or another cutting tool.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: To separate fabric with scissors.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Separar o tecido com tesoura.
items.example_sentence_en: Cut the fabric carefully.
items.example_sentence_pt: Corte o tecido com cuidado.
items.professional_context_en: Cut is one of the first process verbs students need in sewing and pattern preparation.
items.professional_context_pt: Cut é um dos primeiros verbos de processo de que os alunos precisam em costura e preparação de molde.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é cortar.

items.definition_en: To bend fabric over itself.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: To bend the fabric and make a new edge.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Dobrar o tecido para fazer uma nova borda.
items.example_sentence_en: Fold one edge of the fabric.
items.example_sentence_pt: Dobre uma borda do tecido.
items.professional_context_en: Fold is central for hems, seam preparation, and fabric handling.
items.professional_context_pt: Fold é central para barras, preparação de costura e manuseio do tecido.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é dobrar.

items.definition_en: To hold fabric together with pins.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: To fix fabric with pins before sewing.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Prender o tecido com alfinetes antes de costurar.
items.example_sentence_en: Pin the fold carefully.
items.example_sentence_pt: Alfinete a dobra com cuidado.
items.professional_context_en: Pin is useful for step-by-step sewing instructions and safe fabric preparation.
items.professional_context_pt: Pin é útil para instruções passo a passo de costura e preparação segura do tecido.
items.translation_notes_pt: Explique como verbo com o sentido de alfinetar.

items.definition_en: To join or work fabric with needle and thread or a sewing machine.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: To make stitches in fabric.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Fazer pontos no tecido.
items.example_sentence_en: Sew a straight line near the edge.
items.example_sentence_pt: Costure uma linha reta perto da borda.
items.professional_context_en: Sew is the main Week 8 process verb for machine or hand stitching.
items.professional_context_pt: Sew é o principal verbo de processo da Semana 8 para costura à máquina ou à mão.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é costurar.

items.definition_en: To apply heat and pressure with an iron to shape or flatten fabric.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: To use an iron carefully to flatten or shape fabric.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Usar o ferro com cuidado para assentar ou dar forma ao tecido.
items.example_sentence_en: Press the hem with an iron.
items.example_sentence_pt: Passe a barra com o ferro.
items.professional_context_en: Press is an important sewing verb and is more technical than simply iron.
items.professional_context_pt: Press é um verbo importante de costura e é mais técnico do que simplesmente iron.
items.translation_notes_pt: Explique que press pode significar passar ou prensar no contexto da costura.

items.definition_en: To find the size or length of something.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: To check how long or wide it is.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Verificar o comprimento ou a largura.
items.example_sentence_en: Measure the fabric first.
items.example_sentence_pt: Meça o tecido primeiro.
items.professional_context_en: Measure supports accurate preparation before cutting and sewing.
items.professional_context_pt: Measure ajuda na preparação precisa antes de cortar e costurar.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é medir.

items.definition_en: To make a visible line or point on fabric.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: To draw a guide line on the fabric.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Fazer uma linha guia no tecido.
items.example_sentence_en: Mark the line with a pencil.
items.example_sentence_pt: Marque a linha com um lápis.
items.professional_context_en: Mark is useful for sewing preparation and the transition into patternmaking language.
items.professional_context_pt: Mark é útil para preparação de costura e para a transição ao vocabulário de modelagem.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é marcar.

items.definition_en: To look at something carefully to see if it is correct.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: To look carefully and confirm it is right.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Olhar com atenção e confirmar que está certo.
items.example_sentence_en: Check the stitches at the end.
items.example_sentence_pt: Verifique os pontos no final.
items.professional_context_en: Check supports quality control language in simple sewing processes.
items.professional_context_pt: Check apoia a linguagem de controle de qualidade em processos simples de costura.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é verificar ou conferir.

vocabulary_groups.title: Tools and sewing objects
vocabulary_groups.description: Core nouns for parts, tools, and objects in a simple sewing sequence.

items.definition_en: The line where two pieces of fabric are joined.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: The joined line of fabric.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: A linha onde dois tecidos se juntam.
items.example_sentence_en: Check the seam carefully.
items.example_sentence_pt: Verifique a costura com cuidado.
items.professional_context_en: Seam is a central beginner sewing word for garment construction and checking work.
items.professional_context_pt: Seam é uma palavra central de costura inicial para construção de roupas e revisão do trabalho.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais útil é costura.

items.definition_en: A small loop or line of thread in sewing.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A sewing point or small thread mark.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um ponto de costura ou marca pequena de linha.
items.example_sentence_en: The stitch is straight.
items.example_sentence_pt: O ponto está reto.
items.professional_context_en: For A2 learners, stitch should stay mostly as a noun in Week 8.
items.professional_context_pt: Para alunos A2, stitch deve aparecer principalmente como substantivo na Semana 8.
items.translation_notes_pt: Explique principalmente como ponto de costura.

items.definition_en: The finished edge at the bottom of a garment or fabric piece.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: The finished bottom edge.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: A borda acabada na parte de baixo.
items.example_sentence_en: Press the hem at the end.
items.example_sentence_pt: Passe a barra no final.
items.professional_context_en: Hem is central for the reading and process-card tasks this week.
items.professional_context_pt: Hem é central para as tarefas de leitura e do cartão de processo nesta semana.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é barra.

items.definition_en: The outside border of a piece of fabric.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: The border of the fabric.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: A borda do tecido.
items.example_sentence_en: Fold one edge of the fabric.
items.example_sentence_pt: Dobre uma borda do tecido.
items.professional_context_en: Edge supports location language for folding, sewing, and pinning.
items.professional_context_pt: Edge apoia a linguagem de localização para dobrar, costurar e alfinetar.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é borda.

items.definition_en: Thin string used for sewing.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: The thin string used to sew.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: A linha fina usada para costurar.
items.example_sentence_en: Cut the thread at the end.
items.example_sentence_pt: Corte a linha no final.
items.professional_context_en: Thread is useful as a familiar sewing noun that supports hand and machine sewing talk.
items.professional_context_pt: Thread é útil como substantivo familiar de costura que apoia a fala sobre costura à mão e à máquina.
items.translation_notes_pt: Explique que aqui line não é usado; a palavra principal é thread.

items.definition_en: A thin pointed tool used for sewing.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: The sharp tool used with thread.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: A ferramenta pontuda usada com linha.
items.example_sentence_en: Use a needle and thread to sew by hand.
items.example_sentence_pt: Use agulha e linha para costurar à mão.
items.professional_context_en: Needle supports tool language and hand-sewing reference.
items.professional_context_pt: Needle apoia a linguagem de ferramentas e a referência à costura à mão.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é agulha.

items.definition_en: A drawn guide mark for cutting or sewing.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A guide mark to follow on the fabric.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Uma marca guia para seguir no tecido.
items.example_sentence_en: Sew along the line.
items.example_sentence_pt: Costure ao longo da linha.
items.professional_context_en: In Week 8, line should usually mean a drawn guide line, not thread.
items.professional_context_pt: Na Semana 8, line normalmente deve significar uma linha guia desenhada, e não linha de costura.
items.translation_notes_pt: Explique que line aqui é linha desenhada no tecido.

items.definition_en: A cutting tool with two blades.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: The tool used to cut fabric.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: A ferramenta usada para cortar tecido.
items.example_sentence_en: Use scissors to cut the fabric.
items.example_sentence_pt: Use a tesoura para cortar o tecido.
items.professional_context_en: Scissors is one of the most important tool words for sewing preparation.
items.professional_context_pt: Scissors é uma das palavras de ferramenta mais importantes para a preparação da costura.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é tesoura; lembre que scissors aparece no plural em inglês.

items.definition_en: Small pointed tools used to hold fabric in place.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: Small tools that hold the fabric before sewing.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Pequenas ferramentas que seguram o tecido antes de costurar.
items.example_sentence_en: Remove the pins after you sew.
items.example_sentence_pt: Retire os alfinetes depois de costurar.
items.professional_context_en: Pins helps learners connect the tool word to the verb pin.
items.professional_context_pt: Pins ajuda os alunos a ligar a palavra da ferramenta ao verbo pin.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é alfinetes.

items.definition_en: A machine used to sew fabric quickly.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: The machine used to sew fabric.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: A máquina usada para costurar tecido.
items.example_sentence_en: Use the sewing machine to sew the line.
items.example_sentence_pt: Use a máquina de costura para costurar a linha.
items.professional_context_en: Sewing machine is a core studio word that students already know from earlier weeks.
items.professional_context_pt: Sewing machine é uma palavra central do estúdio que os alunos já conhecem de semanas anteriores.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é máquina de costura.

items.definition_en: A heated tool used to flatten or shape fabric.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: The hot tool used to press fabric.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: A ferramenta quente usada para passar o tecido.
items.example_sentence_en: Use an iron to press the hem.
items.example_sentence_pt: Use um ferro para passar a barra.
items.professional_context_en: Iron is familiar and helps explain the more technical verb press.
items.professional_context_pt: Iron é familiar e ajuda a explicar o verbo mais técnico press.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é ferro.

items.definition_en: A flexible tape used to measure fabric or the body.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: The flexible tool used to measure.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: A ferramenta flexível usada para medir.
items.example_sentence_en: Use a measuring tape to measure the fabric.
items.example_sentence_pt: Use uma fita métrica para medir o tecido.
items.professional_context_en: Measuring tape supports accurate preparation and links Week 8 to earlier studio-tool language.
items.professional_context_pt: Measuring tape apoia a preparação precisa e liga a Semana 8 à linguagem anterior de ferramentas do estúdio.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é fita métrica.

vocabulary_groups.title: Sequence and instruction language
vocabulary_groups.description: Core process words and instruction phrases for sewing steps.

items.definition_en: At the beginning of a sequence.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: The beginning step word.

items.example_sentence_pt: Primeiro, meça o tecido.
items.professional_context_en: First is a core process marker for simple instructions.
items.professional_context_pt: First é um marcador central de processo para instruções simples.
items.translation_notes_pt: A tradução mais comum é primeiro.

items.definition_en: After the first step.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: The next simple step word.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: A palavra simples para o passo seguinte.

items.example_sentence_pt: Depois, marque a linha.

items.professional_context_en: Next supports step-by-step explanation in speaking and writing.

items.example_sentence_pt: Finalmente, verifique os pontos.
items.professional_context_en: Finally is central for finishing a process clearly.

items.definition_en: A pattern for connecting a tool to an action.
items.learner_friendly_definition_en: A phrase pattern for tool plus action.
items.learner_friendly_definition_pt: Um padrão de frase para ferramenta mais ação.
items.example_sentence_en: Use scissors to cut the fabric.
